2835E5DDBA00426B9F515806C026961C.description: use historical perspectives to analyze issues in the United States from the past and the present; conduct research on a historical issue or topic, identify a connection to a contemporary issue, and present findings (e.g., oral, visual, video, or electronic presentation, persuasive essay, or research paper); include causes and consequences of the historical action and predict possible consequences of the contemporary action.

5AB414EECDB844A5A9D1402E7B721D2F.description: Use the historical perspective to investigate a significant historical topic from U.S. History Eras 3-6 that also has significance as an issue or topic in the United States today.

366C3CA8CC5C4F8582D5E10C33FC8D20.description:
America at Century's End-compare and contrast the United States in 1800 with the United States in 1898, focusing on similarities and differences in:
  • territory.
  • population.
  • systems of transportation.
  • governmental policies promoting economic development.
  • economic change.
  • the treatment of African-Americans.
  • the policies toward Indigenous Peoples.

AA30EAF34E484B469FA04573531EE489.description: Analyze the major changes in communication, transportation, demography, and urban centers, including the location and growth of cities linked by industry and trade, in the last half of the 19th century.

FB2BDB03539C4469A5437291E9B95384.description: USHG Era 6: The Development Of An Industrial, Urban, And Global United States (1870-1930)

2DE7AAFC10804072BE3E42B7BBE0D513.description: Explain the decision to remove Union troops from the South in 1877 and investigate its impact on Americans.

A4DFBB137091457CBBDC05A4851D4AAE.description: Analyze the intent and the effect of the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments to the Constitution.

E08AAC85BDA24C44B4FCD909FE7B38D1.description: Describe the new role of African-Americans in local, state, and federal government in the years after the Civil War and the national and regional resistance to this change, including the Ku Klux Klan.

5758B19BD19B446CBE415056B6A337AA.description:
Describe the early responses to the end of the Civil War by describing:
  • the policies of the Freedmen's Bureau.
  • the restrictions placed on the rights and opportunities of freedmen, including racial segregation and Black Codes.

E7CB9D595ABA43388D1A4AD767981149.description: Compare the different positions concerning the reconstruction of Southern society and the nation, including the positions of President Abraham Lincoln, President Andrew Johnson, Republicans, Democrats, and African-Americans.

B538A59BBB33443F8AE2884B233C2629.description: Using evidence, develop an argument regarding the character and consequences of Reconstruction.

D0860AAEB0F5494A9B07C186F2EA8C3C.description: Construct generalizations about how the war affected combatants, civilians (including the role of women and Indigenous Peoples), the physical environment, and the future of warfare, including technological developments.

458E10991EEF4A6DAF0F9B57CE6AF48E.description: Describe the role of African-Americans in the war, including black soldiers and regiments, and the increased resistance of enslaved people.

0FCC6C19204B40E99F0BF2F92B1E0C4D.description:
Examine Abraham Lincoln's presidency with respect to:
  • his military and political leadership.
  • the evolution of his emancipation policy (including the Emancipation Proclamation).
  • The role of his significant writings and speeches, including the Gettysburg Address and its relationship to the Declaration of Independence.

5D3092FD4C3A4943A8B166620FE1C340.description:
Make an argument to explain the reasons why the North won the Civil War by considering the following:
  • critical events and battles in the war.
  • the political and military leadership of the North and South.
  • respective advantages and disadvantages of each side, including geographic, demographic, economic, and technological.

971BB332A31345D9951C6A73A41070D4.description: Discuss the social, political, economic, and cultural reasons for secession.

A74C18E99B3A460DA88231981BE91CCB.description: Evaluate the multiple causes, key events, and complex consequences of the Civil War.

B89E1F41D819406DBB720545865043E1.description: Describe how major issues debated at the Constitutional Convention, such as disagreements over the distribution of political power, rights of individuals (liberty and property), rights of states, the election of the executive, and slavery, help explain the Civil War.

F8071688EBEB49F3ACC207206BCD8802.description: Describe the resistance of enslaved persons and effects of their actions before and during the Civil War.

56C95F4C1B7A4271A88488A777A8B222.description:
Draw conclusions about why the following increased sectional tensions:
  • the Missouri Compromise (1820).
  • the Wilmot Proviso (1846).
  • the Compromise of 1850, including the Fugitive Slave Act.
  • the Kansas-Nebraska Act (1854) and subsequent conflict in Kansas.
  • the Dred Scott v. Sandford decision (1857).
  • changes in the party system.

A944410018814DA89D324BD8144AFD82.description: Describe the competing views of John C. Calhoun, Daniel Webster, and Henry Clay on the nature of the union among the states.

B41E74E4C47C425E8D3AAFA34141BB4B.description: Describe the impact of the Northwest Ordinance on the expansion of slavery.

F2C1E02F6E64479899FD0C7359FA25B4.description: Compare the differences in the lives of free black people (including those who escaped from slavery) with the lives of free white people and enslaved people.

2C959DFE6070460DBE4DC2F28CEDD24C.description: Analyze and evaluate the early attempts to abolish or contain slavery and to realize the ideals of the Declaration of Independence.

3C32101ED7104324A367B99B00F40B3D.description: USHG Era 5: Civil War And Reconstruction (1850-1877)

160B4B46C5984D6ABCCB33FF7D6A6638.description: Investigate the role of religion in shaping antebellum reform movements.

CE8C1553218540CF938C4D0DCA2DDE61.description: Analyze the goals and effects of the antebellum temperance movement.

8A70DFDCB30846418C76D47400A99A57.description: Analyze the antebellum women's rights (and suffrage) movement by discussing the goals of its leaders and comparing primary source documents from this era to the Declaration of Independence.

A6A13CFAD3CE430D809E0583E3A6690E.description: Describe the formation and development of the abolitionist movement by considering the roles of key abolitionist leaders and the response of southerners and northerners to the abolitionist movement.

28E7A88499BC4DB08D02818CC4746C80.description: Explain the origins of the American education system.

22B05C30461249408B6A8414EB8DF94F.description: Analyze the growth of antebellum American reform movements.

54A5ECF04AF2453DA1FB3255F75B72EB.description: develop an argument based on evidence about the positive and negative consequences of territorial and economic expansion on Indigenous Peoples, efforts to maintain and sustain the institution of slavery, and the relations between free and slave-holding states.

1D3DB9766C764788B292ED2910E4548B.description: analyze the annexation of the west through the Louisiana Purchase, the removal of Indigenous Peoples from their ancestral homelands, the Mexican-American War, the growth of a system of commercial agriculture, and the idea of Manifest Destiny.

FC579841DA6C4CF3806106B1FC4341BF.description: explain the ideology of the institution of slavery, its policies, and consequences.

13511FE3AE3B43919CFA6EE7D14B1647.description:
compare and contrast the social and economic systems of the Northeast, the South, and the Western Frontier (Kentucky, Ohio Valley, etc.) with respect to geography, climate, and the development of:
  • agriculture, including changes in productivity, technology, supply and demand, and price.
  • industry, including the entrepreneurial development of new industries, such as textiles.
  • the labor force, including labor incentives and changes in labor forces.
  • transportation, including changes in transportation (steamboats and canal barges) and the impact on economic markets and prices.
  • immigration and the growth of nativism.
  • race relations.
  • class relations.

14285AA253554E65936C6B83C61E31B8.description: Describe and analyze the nature and impact of territorial, demographic, and economic growth in the first three decades of the new nation, using maps, charts, and other evidence.

84BD99AE094745E8B4000F45801344FF.description: use Marbury v. Madison to explain the development of the power of the Supreme Court through the doctrine of judicial review.

2D17EF595C5948F3A6300672397387E9.description: examine the origins and intentions of early American political parties, including how they emerged, who participated, and what influenced their ideologies.

AD7FED75BD8A494EBD45C8EE58F3CD4E.description: assess the changes in America's relationships with other nations by analyzing the origins, intents, and purposes of treaties.

18EAF0FBA8FF4E9B96CC488D15715EDA.description: use President George Washington's farewell address to analyze Washington's perspective on the most significant challenges the new nation faced.

6BDF0099D31E43A49522E678CC1820C0.description: Analyze the challenges the new federal government faced and the roles of political and social leaders in meeting those challenges.

87493086E0C04F1E89F522239EDEB5F7.description: Use important ideas and documents to describe the philosophical origins of constitutional government in the United States with an emphasis on the following ideals: social contract, limited government, natural rights, right of revolution, separation of powers, bicameralism, republicanism, and popular participation in government.

6220F2C3E955465FB46B3FCC00095F29.description: Explain how the Bill of Rights reflected the concept of limited government, protection of basic freedoms, and the fear among many Americans of a strong central government.

EE237D9C7AE5472C881A82DF62805E7D.description: Analyze the debates over the ratification of the Constitution from the perspectives of Federalists and Anti-Federalists and describe how the states ratified the Constitution.

C9A69D75868D498E8F8716765AFB4F3E.description: Explain how the new Constitution resolved (or compromised) the major issues, including sharing and separation of power and checking of power among federal government institutions; dual sovereignty (state-federal power); rights of individuals; the Electoral College; the Three-Fifths Compromise; the Great Compromise; and relationships and affairs with tribal nations.

1117BB18288840D19EE4A26136E5A9AC.description: Describe the major issues debated at the Constitutional Convention, including the distribution of political power among the states and within the federal government, the conduct of foreign affairs, commerce with tribes, rights of individuals, the election of the executive, and the enslavement of Africans as a regional and federal issue.

16967F72569B44A2988995D9C4482D91.description: Identify economic, political, and cultural issues facing the nation during the period of the Articles of Confederation and the opening of the Constitutional Convention.

F5BAD1C264E04AD2BBB4C6301DA2AD2C.description: Explain the reasons for the adoption and subsequent failure of the Articles of Confederation.

E55F9552B19E445BB8AF9B47DCFE4796.description: Explain the challenges faced by the new nation and analyze the development of the Constitution as a new plan for governing

3DE85529F26A478A90A548841782F4A1.description: USHG Era 3: Revolution And The New Nation

4F57FC1C4FF54EEEA5134EE32DD1934D.description:
Describe the consequences of the American Revolution by analyzing and evaluating the relative influences of:
  • establishment of an independent republican government.
  • creation of the Articles of Confederation.
  • changing views on freedom and equality.
  • concerns over the distribution of power within government, between government and the governed, and among people.

002CA3C6EA7842459C9FAFC0C0B315D1.description:
Using the Declaration of Independence, including the grievances at the end of the document, describe the role this document played in expressing:
  • colonists' views of government.
  • their reasons for separating from Great Britain.

D3EA84E642FD46158ADA8573DB1B94A6.description:
Describe the ideas, experiences, and interactions that influenced the colonists' decisions to declare independence by analyzing:
  • colonial ideas about government.
  • experiences with self-government.

CBEA35E041B3453A9664758E374E11F2.description: Foundations In U.S. History And Geography Eras 1-2

211C4975536C40A4A93661A03EA4019C.description: assess the financial risk of lost income, assets, health, or identity, and determine if a person should accept the risk exposure, reduce risk, or transfer the risk to others by paying a fee now to avoid the possibility of a larger loss later.

4CA7DC95E4D34D9FB3185677893CC060.description: analyze the risks, expected rate of return, tax benefits, impact of inflation, role of government agencies, and importance of diversification when investing in financial assets.

137D1FC614854FFF92F4C04440158B48.description: evaluate the benefits, costs, and potential impacts of using credit to purchase goods and services.

5D2332443FD84397AE7CFD00B00A4F6B.description: identify the incentives people have to set aside income for future consumption, and evaluate the impact of time, interest rates, and inflation upon the value of savings.

CA7C137A03924E469B1B43E29AA29245.description: describe the factors that consumers may consider when purchasing a good or service, including the costs, benefits, and the role of government in obtaining the information.

504BE1707BBF44009A867A707158F6F4.description: conduct research regarding potential income and employee benefit packages, non-income factors that may influence career choice, benefits and costs of obtaining the necessary education or technical skills, taxes a person is likely to pay, and other possible sources of income.

6FB5A0E47FD946FB99B54EBA2676F7B1.description: analyze and describe how the global economy has changed the interaction of buyers and sellers.

F004B39F298348DCBE964804ED160DA9.description: analyze the effects on trade from a change in an exchange rate between two currencies.

0A8BA7EA0AB74D3CBC9316D59B809DD2.description: assess the impact of trade policies, monetary policy, exchange rates, and interest rates on domestic activity and world trade.

097D1F22CEB249C5A194C374A6CCEEC8.description: use the concepts of absolute and comparative advantages to explain why goods and services are produced in one nation or locale versus another.

60CDC328E4C04F19A816E161D345099A.description: analyze the impact of transitional economies, such as in China and India, on the global economy in general and the American economy in particular.

7D14C8A047EA4DDD9541DE6FEE7196DF.description: compare and contrast the characteristics, advantages, and disadvantages of traditional, command, market, and mixed economic systems.

E3A3CEC5A50B4D8AA51AB385C97F7D4C.description: evaluate the diverse impact of trade policies of the World Trade Organization, World Bank, or International Monetary Fund on developing economies of Africa, Central America, or Asia, and on the developed economies of the United States and Western Europe.

9F0FA412B1EE46C1976FBE68CC8BFFB5.description: assess how factors such as availability of natural resources, investments in human and physical capital, technical assistance, public attitudes and beliefs, property rights, and free trade can affect economic growth in developing nations.

4CEE7FC1B79D46B18219A1AE54055C3C.description: explain the roles and responsibilities of the Federal Reserve system and compare and contrast the consequences (intended and unintended) of different monetary policy actions of the Federal Reserve Board as a means to achieve macroeconomic goals of stable prices, low unemployment, and economic growth.

4EADB0658F36470B9ABF721A273C0E8F.description: analyze the consequences (intended and unintended) of using various tax and spending policies to achieve macroeconomic goals of stable prices, low unemployment, and economic growth.

C12132ACA8CC45999176DA1A6E19BC11.description: evaluate the ways in which the federal government generates revenue on consumption, income, and wealth, and uses that revenue to supply government services and public goods, and protect property rights.

A6C28E43A6B34DDC96AFD4B9693CB508.description: evaluate the three macroeconomic goals of an economic system (stable prices, low unemployment, and economic growth).

983CDE0CF33C4C0B9721B292A7C55319.description: using a number of indicators, such as gross domestic product (GDP), per capita GDP, unemployment rates, and consumer price index, analyze the current and future state of an economy.

831DD7C4F5944F9FA1413F81705E3568.description: using the concept of circular flow, analyze the roles of and relationship between households, business firms, and government in the economy of the United States.

B7CA1FD52AA14584A43E76787893234E.description: The National Economy of the United States of America

7286F7238A794979B1542609728E1BE5.description: analyze the impact of price ceilings and price floors on the quantity of a good or service supplied and demanded in a market.

0B03823B9F6B4EC6BAE8A9834D8887DD.description: assess the incentives for political leaders to implement policies that disperse costs widely over large groups of people and benefit small and politically powerful groups.

8709DAFE944844D798DF9711A7D6ED7F.description: explain the role for government in addressing both negative and positive externalities.

006D3728392F420784F6A8C55BEA209A.description: analyze the ways in which local and state governments generate revenue and use that revenue to supply public services.

A9136FF0C9FE44BD82D6266AFEB464C6.description: analyze the role of government in protecting consumers and enforcing contracts (including property rights), and explain how this role influences the incentives (or disincentives) for people to produce and exchange goods and services.

E5F791EBA0204988B8B7DAFB0B827892.description: analyze the impact of a change in public policy on consumers, producers, workers, savers, and investors.

C2DCFFB625224C9BAC65C0002E7ECFEC.description: analyze how prices change through the interaction of buyers and sellers in a market, including the role of supply, demand, equilibrium, and elasticity, and explain how incentives (monetary and non-monetary) affect choices of households and economic organizations.

A5443D25B71F4A03BFB1F8F334100778.description: use the laws of supply and demand to explain household and business behavior.

F519D22694AC4A2BA9C6EDCE4BF80E4A.description: identify the characteristics of perfect competition, monopolistic competition, oligopoly, and monopoly market structures.

8B33FF53086942338E7AD238A9F61E61.description: describe the roles of various economic institutions and purposes they serve in a market economy.

C36E92207F79404191DA3A7E2FA694F7.description: weigh marginal benefits and marginal costs in decision making.

439A390FF6144FEAA115CEB32DFB4DA3.description: analyze the risks and rewards of entrepreneurship and associate the functions of entrepreneurs with alleviating problems associated with scarcity.

4720B200BD9944CAA8B57AA6AF7CFDA5.description: using examples, explain how scarcity, choice, opportunity costs, and incentives affect decisions made by households, businesses, and governments.

DA3ED7B7E0554B5FAA2BA8ADA2A04C6E.description: Equip students with the skills and knowledge to explore multiple pathways for knowledgeable, civic engagement through simulations and/or real world opportunities for involvement.

611EE6174F9F4E0FBD1762E7EBC75C9C.description: Identify and describe a local, state, national, or international public policy issue; research and evaluate multiple solutions; analyze the consequences of each solution and propose, defend, and take relevant action to address or resolve the issue.

8656938F13204AC096F78F8C233021E2.description: Identify, discuss, and analyze methods individuals and/or groups have chosen to attempt social and legal change. Assess the effects of civil disobedience, social movements, demonstrations, protests on society and law.

0ACC536614C34DAEBB6DDB49BC778AC4.description: Explain and evaluate how people, individually or collectively, seek to bring the United States closer to its Democratic Values.

415AC3CEB7A04DEF8A6367DD5B8C7307.description: Explain how informed members of society influence civic life.

E19D497879FE411896ACCE7FEA02F108.description: Explain the personal dispositions that contribute to knowledgeable and engaged participation in civic communities.

26A861DCD04B4287AEB216A548D36BBB.description: Using examples, explain the rights and responsibilities of U.S. citizens as well all people living in the United States.

10630EB508D942E2B5BAFABCDE433F1D.description: Compare and contrast rights and representation among U.S. people and citizens living in states, territories, federal districts, and on tribally governed land.

49469ACCB4864D63A97368D4A784E4C6.description: Explain how the United States has limited and expanded citizenship over time.

A77D2694340441AD9FC7D0805250C9F6.description: Describe and evaluate the requirements and process for becoming a citizen of the United States.

4265FF38716E4F4990DC818C4A02C366.description: Citizenship and Civic Participation in the United States of America

60272CCBF9BE442480C08C6C7B090503.description: Identify and evaluate international non-governmental organizations.

26EFBDE99A1C448A9283D35AFC237907.description: Identify and evaluate the roles and responsibilities of the United States in international governmental organizations including bilateral and multilateral agreements.

706E4BB64BA14BA4893F527D9CD4DC3B.description: Analyze how international political, economic, technological, and cultural developments impact U.S. institutions and individuals.

8BC8D93A796D4B2CB188FAF488D98CCF.description: Analyze the influence and impact of U.S. political, economic, technological, and cultural developments on countries and people around the world.

4C669D96BF87496597449A364F3073CA.description: Describe ways in which groups and individuals influence foreign policy.

C0A35EC9BE5145CEBE3CD18F75CFB384.description: Analyze past and present examples of U.S. foreign policy, its implementation, and its impact on American and international institutions and individuals.

8185AD0BF2B24361840E790AD999A7E4.description: Identify and describe ways in which foreign policy is made including Constitutional powers of the executive, legislative, and judicial branches and how those powers have been clarified or interpreted over time.

DF36007887954FD8BC42942F7EB6583B.description: The United States of America and World Affairs

E48F55D294404EA19689198AAB089FFD.description: Describe considerations, criteria, and examples that have been used to deny, limit, or extend protection of individual rights.

F7385FAEA8C540D7BB9B6B2C9584AD00.description: Identify and explain personal rights, political rights, and economic rights as well as how these rights might conflict.

5706D79F106F4F48B09E966A0A74BBD4.description: Using the Fourteenth Amendment, describe the impact of the doctrine of incorporation, due process of law, and equal protection of law on the articulation and extension of rights.

07EEA3AE4EDD49C9A26943FE6A1FBCAD.description: Explain how significant historical events, including but not limited to the suffrage movements and the civil rights movements, resulted in changes to the interpretation of and Amendments to the U.S. Constitution.

4A141A6DF34B4C038D5645B7885946D7.description: Explain how the Civil War led to the creation of the Thirteenth, Fourteenth, and Fifteenth Amendments to the U.S. Constitution. Analyze each Amendment's relative effectiveness.

9551DFCC801843BE85CD3C17C534EA31.description: Using the Fourth, Fifth, Sixth, Seventh, and Eighth Amendments, describe the rights of the accused; using court cases and examples, describe the limit and scope of these rights.

9F24060B7495491A84300485E3D7F7AB.description: Describe the five essential rights protected by the First Amendment. Through the use of court cases and examples, explore and analyze the scope and limits of First Amendment rights.

9A8F8C1D7BD0477DBC01CB95841B162D.description: Rights and Liberties in the United States of America

AD6F6931E8354D0EB981F8CE1FD40228.description: Analyze the credibility and validity of various forms of political communication.

EECFAAB0FBEE43A29AE010D422C1A327.description: Explain functions and possible influence of various news and other media sources in political communication.

3F28A7FC296C4A08B3886C9DAED87902.description: Identify and discuss roles of non-governmental organizations in American civic society.

AC99B2F32821484DBC817F108F355F40.description: Show a preference for where to sit during large group time.

FD804E7F07524AF09F63F0633C02C048.description: Save a seat for a friend.

16DE7EECCD7F4A0DA4B7F3D2F80A0B34.description: Bring a favorite book or toy from home to show others.

AAA4C33CEA7D41C88B06C826180E5D72.description: Ask to use alphabet stamps from the writing area so they can finish their painting.

B584859AA71A42608CCDBD84F1A0DDA5.description: Repeatedly ask for the same story to be read.

5881E7E08E2D4BCD8717A49512772F54.description: Share stories about what their family did over the weekend.

0B204F9128FC4981915CA50B5AF1E135.description: Express and share their own interests, ideas, or opinions freely.

D02FF3B918D64D25892F79757F10AC8B.description:
Children engage in explorations and interactions with
confidence.

3D8B0289E0E743669884D9CA85BE16D8.description:
Guess how long it will take for a snowball to melt after they bring it inside,
and then set a timer to test their prediction.

A4AFCC90042B4626B5E5C4B6FB35DD58.description: Use art scraps to build a bridge.

5532C7B03910462FA85E95B6B03F4220.description: Suggest a new ending to a familiar story.

46BB2AD663F8457182614A5F59832AC8.description:
Participate in a discussion about what plants need to grow and draw pictures
of the way the seed they planted is growing.

CA93581C6B7F4A9D80E1425DDB20C869.description: Capture a caterpillar to have as a pet.

31176C037B4C40A2881BD5FC08418203.description: Suggest that two friends arguing over a toy can take turns with it.

A50F711FF34945E3BDEC869D31A2A0CA.description:
With adult support, predict that a car going down a ramp will go faster than
one rolling across a flat floor.

C635DA11BD63479B8C9505601D8D7DA7.description:
Take a connecting-block construction apart and put it back together in a new
way.

F17C26D568D549DEA97CA697A87A01AC.description: Stack blocks to make a tower.

C2F7213F3AA943888D2378A43D86417C.description: Propose and explore possibilities for how things work, what they might do, or what they might be.

6D744575ACE2439099DB8F97631881E3.description:
Set up chairs and other props to represent an experience they’ve had, such
as being on an airplane, and ask other children to pretend to be characters
like the flight attendant, pilot, and passengers.

80CC079BD25B4B95BC13C0EC62EFC146.description: Build a crib out of blocks to use in pretend play.

DFF1DF5153AC47C3A5FBF34BCDA82494.description: Use a stuffed animal as a “baby” in pretend play.

FA2762A3E4DA48D2B4AD1AECE14A303C.description: Make up stories, songs, and dances.

D022713CDA6446ED90C7031B0063907D.description: Sing a song they made up.

7F24F157380D4EABB0BD049659D9B90B.description:
Use yellow and orange paint to paint a picture of how sunny it was
yesterday.

1F7AC3F8741041F68BFD60134A273DD5.description: Demonstrate imagination and creativity in their play.

BD36C3F828E44912B97ED1B6704E6438.description:
Collaborate with other children to develop, share, and follow rules or
expectations in their play together.

40C123B67085465C91F0584616138C26.description: Propose ideas to expand a block city by adding a fire station.

691899AC3DBE4FE39A24ADACCB819F8D.description:
During interactive and shared writing experiences, contribute to the group
story without speaking over other children.

8A2635D5BF7642AF89F7C348CC5B0355.description: Listen to other children share their journal entries.

2042493C97434A67B26C91D03F048AFA.description:
Suggest that a child joining the play can be “the uncle” or “another
superhero.”

104602BBA6624A48BEA2ED2C1993C031.description:
Follow a suggestion that they will pretend to be superheroes rescuing
someone in their outdoor play.

6AB96AACD6664E2B887AFE35EDFEAFB4.description:
Pass dishes during a family-style meal and wait for another child to pour the
juice.

142F1392379F42B7B5BD31D52F9184BC.description: Wait until a timer goes off to signal their turn at the computer.

B39AAB61AE854567B56C74D4890404D6.description: Play a simple board game with other children.

3129D9D18E7D4F94B7A7FC486A544558.description: Accept invitations from other children to join in their games and pretend play.

2566BDDA7A2E400C9A82D9CB902FD144.description: Invite other children to join in pretend play or games.

9CF60E68498B4586BC90000039391B78.description: Begin to show preferences in who they play with.

7A0C5806558C441FA96A3F2EB121BCEF.description: Wait for their turn in a line to go down the slide.

9FC50ABB0E96460783618F86451D7D7E.description:
Play with blocks “with” another child, but without coordinating what they are
each building.

E7A8518B0B75438C9017726CE84F784E.description: Initiate, join, and take turns in play with others.

380A2B394BC041B988FECFBCC6377472.description: Children demonstrate increasingly complex play styles.

C94483AC4ED940D98332B7F3C9F50C15.description:
Recognize that each child has their own likes and dislikes. For example:
“Sierra doesn’t like peas, but I do!”

F96D0CA9575D4466BF7A79565950D01C.description:
Use the correct names of different types of dinosaurs—identifying something
as “a stegosaurus” rather than “a dinosaur.”

B418A63D73A546C18200DED46D5B1AC9.description:
Read and request stories about people going camping after their family
plans a camping trip.

D592D9B2C7CE4A1F9BE0525B636DE218.description:
Adapt their behaviors based on the setting and situation – such as being
quiet in a library or running on the playground.

D8CDBC8D56A34D528B13B0352A9C467D.description:
When looking at pictures of everyone’s families, ask another child, “Is that
your dad in that picture? This is a picture of my mom!”

8F7960FB174E4D61B50C93BB65356F80.description:
Discuss and compare the ways their family is the same as and different from
others. “I have two sisters, but you only have one.”

43697B9997BE473BACC0818BC4307F87.description: Try a new food they’re hesitant about it and discover they like it.

F6D5D33CFBFF40898CD5C55251344C62.description:
Notice that someone has changed their hair cut or color and tell others about
it.

CB9209FB049C479E81A6A1F13A4A5106.description: Repeat or copy friends’ words and actions.

4F8ED6F761EC4FD48803FB6434A3C7D1.description: Reconstruct their ideas about the world around them based on new thoughts and information.

293B69883C404BDE952366155D52B0D9.description: Pull a toy car backward across the floor to find out if it will roll forward on its own.

A438E9FD713644AFA9AAD7F72171085D.description: Use a magnifying glass to look at varying leaf patterns.

2EBB3A6CA8B64FE291A6F50BBC5D315D.description:
Use digital technology and/or books to find information about astronauts and
space.

B4DED2EEA7514F2C98B463DCB7B0A2E1.description:
Ask questions about their observations, and other things that interest
them, such as “Why are the leaves yellow?” and “Why don’t you like to eat
oranges?”

CF59B9048BEE41F6B7C68BB3FC902369.description: Use twigs and rocks to build a small structure.

E28EDC56B69C42289721F2F7D07C5E81.description: Try using blocks of different sizes to balance a scale.

2BBEAFE03B824473831916ADAF4DB491.description: Ask a familiar adult why another child is crying.

A48511B9267C45678C5CE608F7D9F4EC.description: Mix colors together when painting and notice how the colors change.

4B2D1B25E1144A5692C4E247E2A15BC7.description: Throw a ball straight down at the sidewalk to see how high it will bounce.

94440A5B8FE943CEAB4C9624AF6764EE.description: Watch the ants move around in an ant farm.

CFFF0039A6914B928BB525DE729B338C.description: Explore, investigate, and ask questions about the world around them.

C7F830C038114DAAA75C990B87CF825D.description: Assign roles as part of pretend play.

4666688A29E74D1CBB9E016BDF17D6A0.description:
Use interactive technology and/or other materials to create a story with other
children.

19A86D896BA4405B8BF39FE8653E6C1E.description: Use props as part of pretend play.

6CDE4F866F654D669D8F2187C35482D5.description: Ask other children to join them in pretend play.

C7BBF31CE3E846E588B15390DFCBA9F0.description: Pretend to be a firefighter when playing with dramatic play props.

2183BF0A8C614C4592C8609049E7A287.description: Play “house” or other pretend games alongside other children.

20C27BDD005144659DC0E024D90F44CD.description: Use felt pieces to recreate a story told by an adult.

A9A8D764C13C4D33BD07A66CA39CA2FA.description: Use play to interpret and understand the world around them.

4FEDC06F99094AC5AC8633B88D83768F.description:
Children learn about themselves and the world around them through purposeful
play.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

F45F0EBB32484285B8727BA2350B5083.description: Put their own belongings away without prompting, most of the time.

19C728A297C44303B3CE177A70D32FCC.description: Offer help to peers when they notice someone is struggling with an activity.

AD8AA2B2C4F243159A07695FE8C257BA.description:
Care for the environment with increasing responsibility and skill (e.g.,
cleaning up, wiping the table, flushing the toilet, helping others).

D6AA398263D74AAB9E9DA98021631E99.description:
Continue to follow expectations or boundaries set in varying situations, most
of the time.

64C0A0052271404AB6B2720152A49F21.description:
Participate in a group discussion to decide on expectations for the learning
environment and offer detailed suggestions.

3F7CA871E1224949B15D8CEE3D00ED33.description: Put their own belongings away with prompting.

0CD64FBE4C5E49A2A155A95B9F996C59.description:
Show increasing comfort in taking on different roles in their environment
(e.g., helping others, turning off the water, holding the door).

CEAABEA848764EE69AA9093FBF7075AB.description: Follow expectations or boundaries set in varying situations, most of the time.

A8E95C1549854C0B90D2C65313695709.description:
Repeat the language of a particular expectation when they see another child
acting outside that boundary.

4D0F09A0EB4A4044B5A2FA9BA4BD030F.description:
Participate in a group discussion to decide on expectations in the learning
environment.

8D042AA7290148CE95255E6AC252E4B4.description:
Engage with their day-to-day routines with increasing levels of interest,
participation, and responsibility, such as taking on the role of “gardener” to
water the plants or offering their opinion on which of two story choices they
should read as a group.

341E0806D75345D0810C5382DBB482FB.description:
Express spontaneous affection–running up to give a hug, for example–to the
people with whom they spend a lot of time.

47645C499BA24776B25310088A588ADE.description:
Show a desire to positively participate in their community (family, learning environment, school,
community) through showing care and consideration for others.

D588AC8F1BF847B4B322F8C3338120B4.description:
Verbalize or demonstrate their internal debate around whether or not to
break a rule or follow expectations – “I want more crackers, but Mr. Taylor
told me to wait.”

C1981D1CF2194D1AB88B71C61F52325D.description:
Recognize and express frustration or confusion about the differences
between their own families’ expectations and the expectations of other
families for their children – “But Salim’s mom lets him do it!”

5EDAD01A2B8A4A11B821C1C98E06D676.description:
Question a familiar adult’s instructions (“Why do I have to do that?”) while
another child quietly and immediately complies.

30C5983EA3E940B09BBC54909C260380.description:
Expresses frustration when boundaries or expectations are not applied
consistently – “That’s not fair” and “Why can’t I do that too?”

BE287C1A400943FFACF29B608EE006A1.description:
ell a familiar adult when other children aren’t following expectations or
boundaries, such as “Arisa didn’t put the markers away.”

D0AD0AB958554A2A80A7E8C4B33AD285.description:
Inform other children of an expectation they’re not following, for example
“You can’t climb on that!”

9B094E7394164BE2B309166B62A31725.description:
Point out that they are “allowed” to do something or behave a certain way in
another situation – “But Papa says I can!”

1A931F736EB741069501BEE36A0F1129.description:
Begin to make choices that reflect their understanding of fairness and unfairness, as well as the
boundaries and expectations of various situations.

468AFC3573EE42AE80DFE51A8F76D3CC.description:
Children demonstrate an awareness of the ways their choices and actions
may impact the emotional and physical well-being of themselves and others.

461F7642B5AD40CBB896589023A793C9.description: Seek out a familiar adult when they need help to resolve a conflict.

8A630C01CA824EDBB306118429019820.description: Apologize for stepping on another child’s toy.

FDC6E2BBDDC6464DAB8984DDA419C430.description: Share, and ask to share, toys with other children, most of the time.

B3B4DF2C8E3D4E3483FBF270EC2D3EE8.description:
Negotiate with other children to decide who will get the first turn, with adult
support.

BC0DAB3431B24EDC9995F8CC70758842.description:
Tell a familiar adult that they are mad, angry, or sad because another child
took the toy they were playing with.

E2A0214252494F86AB5E74A79EDF3204.description:
With reminders, use “belly breathing,” “bunny breathing,” or other techniques
to manage their own emotions during a conflict.

F2E86E3ABFEE412C8AC0C9BFA7953B8E.description:
Express themselves through words or signs and attempt to explain the
whole story of a particular conflict and why they feel this way.

9317CF95161F4E3AA46EAF6E9B2DAEA3.description:
Express disappointment in others by announcing that they “hate” the other
person.

F66499A40ED846D2927759B5401D9EF0.description: Sometimes take turns or work out other small conflicts with other children.

84EAB3B50928462CBB50D071CDCA5167.description:
Suggest ideas to help resolve conflicts. “I’m playing with this doll, but you
can have that one.”

77E42E6BB9E24110893A81FDDD301DB9.description:
With adult support and reinforcement, listen to another child’s perspective
about a conflict, and work together to come up with ideas for a resolution.

73F1C1D56F3D4F68BC309371AD1E576D.description:
With adult support, identify their big emotions and use breathing techniques
to manage them.

D71354FF1ACF4EDF8B7642B0101CC977.description:
Continue to sometimes express emotions physically, such as knocking down
another child’s block tower because that child wouldn’t let them play.

687A51EE56474612B2D2F724CB434BB8.description:
Seek out a familiar adult to explain their interpretations of what is happening
to cause their emotions. “Billy is being mean to me!”

26977A8C5B0B470981EEAACC290FA241.description:
Use signs, words and phrases that have been modeled for them, when
attempting to resolve conflicts. “I don’t like that.”

0A828C1F3D20400A84DD86F16EC271E3.description: Seek out a familiar adult to help resolve conflicts with other children.

17B7F15599F24E09A6504FEB7B5CC49A.description:
With adult support, practice using words or signs to express their feelings, as
well as the reason for a disagreement or conflict, and their ideas for how to
resolve the issue.

3C8C9213F7B9461D8D2B45D408A0F259.description:
Continue to express emotions physically or in big ways, such as shouting
“No!” when they disagree or don’t want to do something.

441BA9FCFAFD43929FD3EB6F13254995.description: Express disagreement and begin to manage conflict in safe, developmentally appropriate ways.

985590D729434DD5951FF439ACE767EA.description:
Form quick connections with other children who have similar interests or
other common ground.

ACBDEF79B3BA43A8A7BB9A1DA33E3B87.description: Engage in conversation and play with unfamiliar children.

E74DB85153F348538CDA052BF0E49012.description: Ask to play with a new friend again.

AD2AA6559F4842A3B3575C9DCC575A07.description:
Engage in play with unfamiliar children and, with reminders, introduce
themselves.

19B9699189854CD9AC2451AC6C61B700.description: Play with the same few children consistently.

A47B10F5C4AA49F38425D6CB1F887D41.description: Stand on the edge of a group of children they would like to join.

53734770C6434F909E64145571B436AA.description:
Ask other children and familiar adults questions about their families and
home lives.

6DD0B099651A4B0B88B583D1AB6F5F12.description: With support and prompting, introduce themselves to unfamiliar children.

DC37C557153640168C90CBD1623B2039.description:
Spontaneously play alongside or join in play with other children, familiar or
unfamiliar.

9E5E5A8F41E5493B96DCB26008F0A1B3.description:
Engage in pretend play that allows them to explore the roles of favorite
adults.

3E8079C4F41C46D6817ACB8F35A2FD04.description: Show preferences for playing with specific children.

BD9FCB545C59441484D0A856E6E9CA7D.description:
Develop and maintain deep, caring connections, friendships, and other relationships with people of
various cultures, family structures, home languages, racial identities, genders and gender identities, abilities and
disabilities, religious beliefs, and socio-economic classes.

7D4896C91E6842A9B5A506249C44F81F.description: Take turns in conversation with other children.

E62D60AC476F454CBF107C4D1FF8FB87.description:
Use new or additional strategies to enter play with others: suggest something to
do together (“Do you want to play hide and seek?”), offer to share a toy, and join
into existing play (“Can I be the dad in the family?”).

479CB05DBBFB4719A78F8B8D154FF411.description:
Maintain and show enjoyment (smiles, laughter, etc.) of positive interactions with
other children.

B2AD7AB4F6F74830A8339BC28E2C910A.description:
Engage in joint play with others, with increasing intentionality, including making
plans for goals, roles, rules, and expectations of their play–and demonstrate
willingness to include others’ ideas in that planning.

0D39FB59A6F342869184274AA6F69A97.description:
Usually engage with adults by saying hello or goodbye without prompting,
respond to requests or directions from familiar adults, and ask or wait for
permission from a familiar adult if they are not sure about something.

E7164D1221784EC094C12F24475AFE75.description: Usually respond to requests and directions from familiar adults.

64F708231A8C4ABABD4FA4E65A164A6C.description: Engage in longer interactions with both familiar and new adults, with more backand-forth communication.

9930F4E0DD954FE5916BE80FA9B402C6.description:
Begin to show interest in the feelings, likes and dislikes, and general wellbeing of
familiar adults.

A52DBF4AB19B48A8880EA7847C6EBEA3.description:
Show excitement or relief when they can make themselves understood in their
home language.

B657218C74334DD4B6D58EAB88ADD64B.description:
Play cooperatively with others with increasing intentionality, including making
plans with other children about what to play and how (the “rules” of their game or
play, for example).

4DC1C4B1125842A6867C2A1B8E48C257.description:
Engage in longer reciprocal (back-and-forth) interactions with adults to talk about
their experiences. For example, a child might tell a familiar adult, “I went to the
zoo!” and then answer a series of questions about what they saw at the zoo.

8095B04F066C4EDEB0BDFEFBD2723359.description:
Engage in simple cooperative play with others and begin to extend the length of
that play..

3740956FE1254CB8B677388DED5C3FDD.description:
Enter play by making suggestions for other children’s play, such as holding out a
lion toy to children building a zoo and saying, “You could put the lion in that one!”

D331A74E5FA44BC997B91F9C7F1BD52D.description:
Begin engaging in social play by mimicking other children’s play, such as when
other children are playing a running game, begin to run and check if they’ve been
noticed and included.

B5B7D65E93D34EE4AA80E6EE3614460D.description: Communicate their own ideas and ask for help when needed.

6199875851CF44B181ADC280B923508C.description: Show preference for certain children and greet them by name.

A2E6A7D8624B4FC590DF51744D9E266E.description:
Demonstrate an ability to initiate and sustain interactions and communication with others, primarily
in their home language.

B1E9A8A9B19E4709B52A6C8299695622.description: Sit near or lean against a trusted familiar adult.

B3C7A546E1E340ECA3B6216406827044.description: Be eager to share their accomplishments with familiar adults.

911BC9FE68C848B3AAE8AAF3E074124D.description: Show comfort and confidence in expressing themselves to familiar adults.

8A85520C8DF045778E0D96F6A1A4BC85.description: Seek out affection from familiar adults.

0530FE26A9874492B9CD6038E60CBE57.description: Look to or ask adults for comfort and help when needed.

8A22A2E180524F748F743083A46E57E1.description: Glance back at familiar adults to reassure themselves they are not “alone.”

A7C639AE787143B4868492585015A26F.description:
Begin to comfortably interact with an increasing number of significant people
in their lives beyond families and primary caregivers.

4016BFEDC9334921996D8425F9B96EC5.description: Demonstrate healthy attachment to and trust in familiar adults in their lives.

FEBD86AE45484857B2FE5D5560C47DEB.description:
Children interact and communicate to form deep, caring connections, friendships, and
other relationships, and to manage conflict.

68362FF05DCA4C6392D8B4B8AFA26DF7.description:
Recognize and name similarities and differences in their roles, expectations,
and behaviors across different groups and settings.

EC981ABBB801474DA3495741C47D6073.description:
Share stories about being part of a different group than the one they’re
talking to. “When I was at the family reunion…”

BFA495D132584EDEA39CB566076AD2C4.description:
Describe themselves and others using multiple characteristics, including
physical features, talents, culture, and interests.

5A5EE9AA2DC244EC869945B39DF9BD05.description:
Ask for help with something from another child because they recognize it is a
strength of the other child.

0D26122A327B43E3B23A1630033A5F09.description:
Identify themselves as being part of various groups, such as their family,
their neighborhood community, their faith, their school community, as well as
their racial, cultural, linguistic, and gender identities.

DAA99A55E78243E5BCD39898563E08C5.description:
Share a story about a family gathering or otherwise describe their
connections to their family and community.

55A184FA1090453495B0FC3313C1C574.description:
Begin to differentiate themselves more clearly from others. “My dad doesn’t
like to fish, but me and my grandpa do.”

DF4176B7C9244E899C6F9ED3099711EA.description:
Show increased understanding that others have differing interests, thoughts,
beliefs, ideas, feelings, and strengths. “Seanan is fast when she runs!”
“Miguel likes to play in the kitchen.”

7DE3B638FF3B4E3AB27402D54CF2C1D5.description:
Draw pictures of their family or share a special object related to their family
traditions or cultural heritage.

A2A8D09210FC4CA08635ACC3FBEBED6E.description:
Describe their interests, ideas, and likes and dislikes when prompted. For
example, responding with a color name when a familiar adult asks which
colors, they want to play with, or answering a question about their favorite
animal.

958963DC84E94C46B9D516E8660E0ED6.description:
Show increased understanding of their own strengths and interests in
contrast to others’. “I’m a good climber!” and “You like purple, but I like
green.”

CB02EA62963842D692F0B954C1F8AB5E.description:
Demonstrate an understanding that the diverse community of people around them have unique
strengths and experiences to share and should be treated with respect.

6B89792D1DA348DB88E9ADC2BA2FBC44.description:
Notice when there is space in a play area for them to join, and recognize
non-verbal cues, such as the other children looking up and smiling at them
when they approach, as a tool to help them decide if they will ask to join.

BB38B50EB14E4F31889BDC613967E10E.description:
Move a toy or chair out of the path of a child in a wheelchair or walking with
leg braces.

3D252DB7FBB84D6486C93F70AB0B9259.description:
Understand the difference between helpful and hurtful ways to get
something or meet a need.

24999EFB839E45E89FEEDD14B831B64C.description: Talk with other children during snack or mealtime.

5662E6E1237744F2B2E94E407337CCA0.description: Begin to play with friends, for example playing games or building together.

E9F39E6F8F644BDEBCF5E71B0BD3FD39.description: Give a hug to a child who is crying.

C059A04B01CA45B1B0A8BB06B55DF47C.description: Comment on what another child is doing.

DE86DF5A61124EE9A6DA6FD939C771D0.description: Wave someone “toward them” to show them something or seek help.

9346E2A83E3F46898ABBC620641D12D5.description:
Understand facial expressions, vocal tone, and physical tension as cues to
engage or not engage with another person.

C954D8537DD24C7AAE4E46D406EE6852.description: Interact with another child who is playing in the block corner alongside them.

D4B01F6334D248B598232EC568B8902C.description: Recognize and respond to social cues.

977DAF1179B24125BC62FE53FED9E4B7.description:
Accurately recognize and label the emotions of others with increasing
consistency, especially those who are familiar, but also growing to include
strangers and those in stories and other media.

C17D2729563344608B0507C3742F6E4B.description:
Begin to respond to others with empathy – “I’m sorry your grandma couldn’t
come to the lunch today, Jordan. You can sit with me and my grandma!”

A8873CEFD6244E26819931795363873B.description:
Try to predict and identify the cause and/or consequence of others’ emotions
in stories, such as “I think the pigs are scared of the wolf, even though
they’re acting brave when they say, ‘not by the hair of my chinny chin chin.’”
or “I think the wolf is getting angry because the pigs are teasing him.”

6A6051C9637B40F7BD99DCC242465DB5.description:
Notice more subtle expressions of emotion from others, such as recognizing
that a child who is standing outside a group of children playing a game might
be shy or nervous to join in.

8A2FEFBE28FE468383C195051CE7A8DA.description:
Briefly try to help someone who is upset by thinking about that person’s
specific needs. For example, Donetta is sad, and Francesca gets Donetta’s
blanket from her cubby to help or goes to tell an adult that Donetta needs
help.

34E0489C144C4087B4059A3529CF1C4C.description:
Try to predict and identify the cause and/or consequence of others’
emotions, such as “My puppy loves me. He barks and wags his tail and licks
me when I come home!”

DD04D83FB6674B8FAABAB006B63041B1.description:
Notice and label, with increasing accuracy, non-verbal indicators of others’
strong feelings, such as “Jalen’s mad!” when another child stomps their foot.

ACDFB4E1B2FD41A7B76FF470EF79B492.description:
Recognize and respond to other children’s expression of strong feelings,
such as laughing when other children are laughing.

2F031B9FE973460D9CF282E4FC07C6DD.description: Recognize other people’s emotions and respond with care, sensitivity, and later empathy.

67457E51C2D14C5ABA61B412C665F146.description:
Children demonstrate a growing ability to show care and understanding for the way
other people feel, and begin to recognize that people may think, feel, and experience things differently from each
other.

E322CEBA65A4442B974B6196C1EEFE8A.description:
Persist in a challenging task, such as putting together a puzzle and working
through trying a puzzle piece in different spots until it fits.

6E7129F152EE426B9B6164543425E456.description: Notice that a chosen activity is “full” and make a different choice.

2AB5178CEF9142EBA597DBCA3AB7C085.description:
Follow routines with little prompting, such as going to put a coat on when a
familiar adult says, “It’s time to go outside.”

F7C0D7531DB24B4EAE9296947CE1067F.description:
Establish and maintain a familiar goodbye routine for separating from a
family member at school, such as turning around at the door to blow a kiss
goodbye.

3CA810AEE1D74633AFD0BE3C7D8FDBA3.description:
When it is time to transition from learning centers to lunch, help carry the
transition sign around to inform their peers.

2F617B26504C4F958853D11D70BB7C57.description:
When a paint stroke spatters across the paper, look to a familiar adult for
reassurance, and then with that support, incorporate the spatters into the
painting as stars or something else.

5265459A03A94FFAAE0CC4AAB6A8789B.description: With support, retry a difficult task.

CC2F8338457A4B8D9E18F2044D7437E5.description: Manage transitions and follow routines most of the time.

40EF7355AE444D70B7FAB6C2C19C7A1D.description:
Tolerate and enjoy a moderate degree of change, surprises, uncertainty, and
potentially puzzling events.

D123607B23A14111857CF24BAC934520.description: Show understanding that they can run on the playground but not indoors.

5EE34C5C8D1249CEA73BB17FD2F1C56D.description:
Demonstrate an understanding that different settings have different routines
and expectations, such as home and school.

8FFCC2542BFC451793C07EBF80D1B66F.description:
Readily cooperate with routines and tasks when provided with the
opportunity to make choices throughout their day.

9C8BB9EA277244E1A24BE3B5EE0485F1.description: Demonstrate flexibility and an increasing ability to adapt to changes and setbacks.

313AAC02546D4D01A8CF81DCCC3D8FFC.description:
Tell a familiar adult that they are mad, angry, or sad because another child took
the toy they were playing with.

192BA28F14DB4F58836A0D27AC430072.description:
Verbally express what they are feeling using a bigger and more detailed
vocabulary, such as saying, “I’m excited because my mom is taking me to
gymnastics today,” or “I’m proud of me and Josie because we built the tallest
tower.”

E1D9DBEDE5174F7F9250CE3E13CD268B.description:
Use “belly breathing,” “bunny breathing,” or other techniques to manage their
own emotions.

A8A7CB9F3167436EB610E2D69DA454DB.description:
Express themselves through words or signs and attempt to explain the whole
story of why they feel the way they do.

76DA14E859AB4892B194DFA7224F7B40.description: Express disappointment by crumpling a paper they made a mistake on.

CE43CE756AFF4CFC952B07F4FC9DBFA8.description:
With adult support, identify their emotions and use breathing techniques to
manage them.

8E524A9BC4FE4957A475537324F28D4B.description: Say, “That was fun!” or “I don’t like that,” after trying a new activity.

F5CFFB774A6F42FE9DB2ACF4182938EE.description: Verbally express what they are feeling.

80EE5B1F3B5F4660B39D103D888DFD9D.description:
Continue to sometimes express emotions physically, such as knocking down
another child’s block tower because that child wouldn’t let them play.

B26B248629934CF98FE478115826D9AF.description:
Seek out a familiar adult to explain their interpretations of what is happening to
cause their emotions. “Billy is being mean to me!”

D02319D614234ABEA7D87CBE65F9AF55.description: Announce that “He’s funny” when laughing at an adult being silly.

24C56054E3524266B661847D051C09F7.description:
With adult support, practice using words or signs to express their emotions,
needs, and wants.

2E97986D99F641DDB8933C601D2AAFB4.description:
Continue to express emotions physically or in big ways, such as squealing and
twirling in a circle, throwing a toy, or shouting “No!”

344BFAB370E84DE2A31E801A403A1247.description:
Express their emotions freely, and begin to identify and manage those emotions, with support from
familiar adults.

0E234F5D50564C8E85EE30D15999088B.description:
Children recognize the connections between their emotions and reactions and begin to
control their impulses in different situations.

0463CFE12F5B45D7B1A80ECFA2BD6D74.description: May resist repeating experiences they were not previously successful with.

7D6627E4A6EA42E5A9ABB58A5DDC58C9.description: Be reluctant to try new things that may require skills they haven’t mastered.

B0E7C8A441FB46798AEF7ACFCFFCF691.description:
Watch other children play for a moment or two to get a sense of what’s
happening and then go to join in

B251F0868F6E4DE89D68C85714CE137F.description:
With encouragement, introduce themselves to an unfamiliar child and go
play with them.

2FC1BE7C6B854C9E9656575805C05738.description: Join a group of familiar children in playing a new game.

13976BD40C4D421696FAC2F4BA58D6CA.description:
Explore new materials or experiences (like a playground structure) with a
familiar child or adult.

0C16B500394242219B4CAAAEBEA99C1C.description:
With encouragement, “join in” with play by sitting down nearby to play with
the same objects (such as building their own tower near someone else’s
construction).

FAA23ABC35D645B68511586C49F53D5B.description: Watch other children’s play with interest.

AC810674BF2E4B2DAA7C30F01A8E37F9.description: Demonstrate willingness to explore independently and try new things.

7338B95061394E839352C8B73699CD4E.description:
Volunteer to explain what the Spanish words in Abuela mean while a familiar
adult reads the story.

B5742E58E84940ADB01B64DD909D1B23.description: Compare their drawing of a tree to the illustration in a book.

16E541F88FD94FE6B51BF5B216DD6F7E.description:
Point out, while a familiar adult reads the book Abuela to the group, that the
Spanish words in the story are the same language they speak at home with
their family.

330685ACE64F49BBB32F27E2CA243D97.description:
Announce successes and accomplishments, such as “Look, I can climb to
the top of the slide!”

03E773BCB773422D8C7556983542FC46.description: Choose picture books from the library that have main characters who look like them.

A8FE682930D249FA8437D179D659F85A.description:
Demonstrate awareness of and recognize the value of their personal traits, including their strengths
and interests.

939BC22A289244C981131305D8FF9AD0.description: Children recognize and value their own individuality, emotions, and strengths.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

D4B9D3ED6BC44BB89971858E528FD23D.description: Point out that people need water to live, just like animals and plants.

29C24CC6A2714D02970AEE70785D83C2.description:
Sort photos of foods into a Venn diagram with categories such as “foods that
are grown in the ground,” “foods that come from animals,” and “both.”

009D800B078D408B857E15AE1F87A22D.description: Point out that yogurt is made from milk, which comes from a cow.

455CB1B59A704797B6C3F22596F0C1F7.description:
Ask a familiar adult if their snack or lunch contains something they are
allergic to.

6CA9EC9B30504C749792012082E7EBE1.description: Help a familiar adult measure and mix to prepare a fruit salad.

9B2F0E7EBF92433EA329672AFBB7E1C3.description: Sort food by food groups–fruit, vegetable, grain, protein, and dairy.

9DBB8C29F29140B791246FC7FDEE026C.description: Tell a familiar adult that drinking water is good for their bodies and brains.

BF041E43DF28459A9BCB2D645885338C.description: Remind a familiar adult that they can’t have pork sausages.

0171C2AECA644BF28EB096D86C9DBBB2.description:
Tell another child or familiar adult that they are allergic to (or “can’t have”)
peanuts.

878544CBEA414C06A03400D828D63EE9.description: Ask if a food is a fruit or vegetable.

9088E7EC1EE44D63BE2FA1996864C3F8.description:
After washing hands, help prepare snack by counting how many people are
eating and making sure there is enough for everyone.

77896CB1D9724D69B8B285FA6EE8DFE9.description: Tell another child that carrots are good for eyesight.

DE8ADF09569643C5A0843E6AC5182909.description:
Identify a variety of foods and livestock that typically come from farms/
ranches.

AAA95FB2AB4043A9A8EDF8A9150B0A71.description: Remind a familiar adult to also grab the ‘special’ milk for them.

BA6263339BA648D383536BE9C69436E6.description: Say, “I can’t eat strawberries because they make my belly feel yucky.”

4A0364F536214330A0CB2910495E457D.description: Help a familiar adult pass out cheese and crackers.

B71FAE890DCB49C9B15A1A5F94059E06.description: Separate play foods into “anytime foods” and “sometimes foods.”

4346EF6F6EC840999D369A891DFA6F8E.description:
Develop an awareness of how foods look, feel, taste, and smell different; how different foods affect
their bodies; and how foods are sorted into food groups.

FB089BE3FC4048E5A60D542B57AC34E0.description:
Ask another child about the unfamiliar food they are eating—what it tastes
like, what’s in it, etc.—most of the time.

DE9757C3D48E4904A3E5BF0B7DCD8205.description: Taste test different fruits they have not eaten before.

7A68843386684F769DAAA7A5DF1F8FBB.description: Sort scented markers in groups of smells they like or do not like.

CC53480AE98D42C2B9135BD022EEB2B4.description: Ask, “What’s that smell?” when lunch is delivered.

ACFF3A63D544415090BA42BDC506137F.description:
With modeling and support, ask another child about the unfamiliar food they
are eating—what it tastes like, what’s in it, etc.—sometimes.

03C82877C13D4C54B442B7E5D2749581.description: Try a new food after watching a familiar adult eat it.

9962CEA7BCBD4781B77BEFB424D6AB76.description:
With modeling and guidance, respond to other children eating unfamiliar
foods as a normal situation, most of the time.

C8F897B3016141FFB7F986D9FE1EE671.description:
Ask a familiar adult about what someone else is eating, when it is a food,
they aren’t familiar with.

419760C8EA5549E7ADDBE2D2F9BFC2E8.description: Sample a variety of apple types.

A029AF0661644F7FB7604389F3E7B494.description: Show interest in new or different tastes, smells, and foods.

B98849AC14274A5688DDF42A63F872C3.description: Ask for water with a meal.

6A7B19371A4B449A982E3287350ED275.description: Fill their own water bottle when it is empty.

1250B9CB057644E4AA731FB59051BA02.description: Get their own snack and sit down to eat it.

47CDDF3193BB4D869FDE8FFEE886CBDE.description: Tell a familiar adult that their belly is growling.

F287829842C74E31A8C95B10BFF57884.description: Say, “I’m full,” before throwing away the trash from their lunch.

EF3205C006FA4D018FC99F9D1B063DB0.description: Forget to drink water when busy with an activity.

7BDCED0E618A4A2F97D007A6F2EE3441.description: Drink independently from an open cup.

D80B4F7FE6694333AD71CC3F509A345A.description:
Make observations during an experiment with plants where one gets water,
and one doesn’t.

05E70984B02046D4B1E6C97FD4DE7492.description: Ask for their water cup to be refilled for a drink.

8ACF8B1AD73C4E2089CBB08144CA5401.description: Get their water bottle when they are thirsty.

2AE34542A62B4C1683CCAA1790BBF0E4.description: Become aware of and respond to feelings of thirst, hunger, and fullness.

7255DBD9EC864AD690D9816221207CF7.description: Children experience and become aware of the ways foods and drinks affect their bodies.

6B004248E73C447EA78CB647D454B6AD.description:
Use scissors to open a package of crackers instead of asking for adult
support.

7CE55E1062AD4CE5923E43C28F89B6B7.description:
Follow routines in the learning environment independently, such as putting
library books in a bin, making lunch choices, and hanging up their coat,
most of the time.

899B047A8F9D4ADB96CF3CE0442B89AE.description:
Count plates and cups to make sure there is enough for everyone to eat
snack.

18521E829DE340139B309403A860DAB2.description: Attempt to dress themselves for the weather before going outside.

D587B56922504A038F0C366D413DF06F.description: Ask for a bandage when they are bleeding.

40C9DC2FF82343989319FEBABE7FB288.description: Pass out cups to each child at snack time.

91D27203080F436AAB07620511A1057C.description: Drink independently from an open cup.

31ABD5E2E881403A82E206C183C25D91.description: Put things in their backpack to go home but forget to close it.

6ADE27BF4EDF41EB9CB3DDD3819FCC3B.description: Start using the bathroom without assistance.

383A24B4E5ED4CAC929956D6E364ABB5.description: Put the end of their zipper in but not yet pull it up.

4FFA09BDAAFD446486A7A0EABF568977.description: Show increasing ability to perform self-care routines and tasks.

21FE945B9F2248F39371DA29B5E89E1C.description: Explain to another child where to go during fire or tornado drills.

DDAAC91215E94B8FB9BDF02245418EC4.description: Identify areas of the playground that are off-limits for children.

F796F7147BC849E69E20B94509A56E28.description: Ask for help getting down if they are too high on a climber.

7ACB707748D542CDA0366D68F5F54DD9.description: Independently put on a bike helmet before getting on their bike.

17A7404E21194C0DBE11451E8E53C201.description:
Wait at a sidewalk intersection until the “WALK” signal lights up, then
look both ways before continuing.

72565426199B4ACF88EC15EFB47DFF27.description:
Tell other children to come to the door and line up when the fire alarm
goes off.

3840288B1B3E40BD9DC1CA158E3EB5B5.description:
Participate in a group discussion of how to be safe and give
examples such as walking when they are inside, respecting others’
bodies and personal space, and staying with their group.

C64AC66EFF324742B70D56273A67DB26.description: Walk with scissors held in a fist grasp.

9E6983F6C1994F4E8F21DA47A8E8FE22.description: Put their hands up to block a child from hitting them.

CC977F1F6328400C88221A3D966240D9.description: Say, “look both ways” before crossing the street with an adult.

172CB5DCE0B149638F39AA23F4D52549.description: Move away from a child who is kicking blocks over.

E2D51CE9DAC34B18B41836A16ACD4295.description: Move away from others at large group time so they have more space.

3211444BEA964A178AA0CA321E0C0798.description: With reminders, line up at the door as the fire alarm is going off.

BA5186871A2944869A5070CA5547B3FB.description: Demonstrate increasing awareness of safe boundaries and safety routines.

184261136FC4443BBE08DF86352E07E4.description:
Approach a familiar adult to announce that they are sick or “don’t feel good”
when they are coughing, have a runny nose, or feel feverish.

207CE8B5F60049DABF87D1D92498653C.description: Sing the alphabet song when they wash their hands.

4C831BF97FE84C62A2199EB2700C8849.description:
Follow handwashing routines independently and without prompting, most of
the time.

B173FFAB4C3B46E5A298DB82E651CCF2.description: Follow handwashing routines independently and without prompting, sometimes.

23C21476FBCD4059B95326D015CE35E5.description: Cough and sneeze into their elbow.

97730B92C48943F0AAA649C0DF004489.description: Tell someone not to touch them after seeing them lick their hand.

3486CA2852FB4F6D9768E3F37A005DA3.description: Get a tissue for another child with a runny nose.

F85509B457FA41AD8409C8B4EFA11A2B.description:
With prompting, wash their hands independently, before and after meals,
after toileting, and after outdoor times.

292BE429245446C488AC862FD9D3425C.description:
Tell a familiar adult they have a runny nose and need a tissue or, sometimes,
feel their nose running and grab a tissue on their own.

5C3BC0CC69134E0991D492CABC702328.description: With reminders, cough, and sneeze into their elbows

17BE07793155465B8BA1C13FDE4AF757.description:
Become aware of ways they can prevent the spread of germs and illnesses, and begin to identify
and manage some symptoms of illness.

0EE6E8AA47CB439FA3F8BC0DFFB73BA4.description:
Follow handwashing routines independently and without prompting, most of
the time.

6CE94DDB603A42F1AE779427869936FF.description:
Communicate why they are upset and brainstorm solutions with a familiar
adult.

60749C2BDBE24585A0FE3CB771D94FD4.description: Eat the healthy part of lunch first and save dessert for last.

7CF75F116C0F4685A769202CD5568E09.description:
Follow handwashing routines independently and without prompting,
sometimes.

05D55504AFF043FF9AEEEB7FABA499FB.description: Say, “I’m going to be tired!” after running around at recess.

A84E3D509993482A8C70A5C42E7E2C65.description: Ask a familiar adult, “Is this healthy for me?”

BDAA0A398E7D4D7789DBB14734DB617B.description:
With prompting, wash their hands independently, before and after meals,
after toileting, and after outdoor times.

7007C4D9F2F4421B98876316A0D63366.description: Run around the playground after having a disagreement with another child.

2B01EEB980D6430FA9B0F48773B74917.description: Pick up a box and announce, “I’m so strong!”

6CDA4D24025247B19CBFFB9A7EB654E1.description:
Begin to understand the connections between physical activity, hygiene, nutrition, emotional
wellness, and physical health.

DCC84497856F4D70BBAA9874343FF213.description:
Children recognize and practice the ways they can support and advocate for
their own needs and the safety of themselves and others.

F29FA152D2F149AEBD3D3847C720DD86.description: Color in a circle they have drawn.

6666A61961D84276B82056653FDEDDD3.description: Hit a ball with a paddle or a bat.

62D42D1688624BA2BFD5518604355E9D.description: Follow a magnetic maze with a magnet stick.

5D96EC9B1EA84AE5B02F5B97F4F0E7B7.description: Use child-safe tweezers to move pom-poms from one bowl to another.

F1CBC8D79DDD45C09501D844D0C49E61.description: Continue to use lacing cards with thinner string and more complex designs.

D4E7F17C5FCB40B3BE15BADAD71F9320.description: Use a mouse to control the cursor on a computer screen.

E7A99787EEA84EC592AFC12693BE87F0.description: Stacking small cubes in a tower.

88F7EE5C31144BEBB8F995F1D2ACA565.description: String smaller beads onto a pipe cleaner.

1D5BEC6B636A4BEE9F04FD39CAFCAAAC.description: String big wooden beads onto shoelaces or pipe cleaners.

CD3AE61B2EEE41FDA946BE3F21EEC227.description: Thread a shoelace or thick string through lacing cards.

88372C16A25A479CB7069876C3BD93D5.description: Place small pegs in a pegboard.

6962F2C38C2B426B9A2B34BBFB125117.description: Stretch rubber bands across a pegboard to make shapes.

451FBDE485614F9E96FBD56BF29B3A3D.description: Stretch small rubber bands around a tongue depressor several times.

AB4A074FE5B844AE9A12B40C7BE9E34A.description: Tighten nuts onto bolts with their fingers.

A2E14C9A2CA744B2951723C14601B156.description: Begin to zip their coat independently.

38D2B4579C024FFE99178CF5BE1F343B.description: Hold a pencil with full control.

0681EC83E76A44B8A67B6FF2D975A12A.description: Begin to follow a predefined path when cutting.

5E73FAD264D74381AA801A3B9F938BAB.description: Squeeze a hole puncher until it successfully punches a hole in paper.

89F14678D08947EF84CBDF3DC43B906B.description: Unzip their coat and finish zipping when someone else gets it started.

08D1FB67EC984EAE94BEFC3F3AE2B111.description: Use scissors to snip paper, and later cut in a line.

001723747F904FD0AFF789AE483066B7.description: Explore and develop more strength and precise control over their hands and fingers.

29F5525A923E413696C0262B7EB06F5A.description: “Blow” their nose independently (one nostril at a time).

1EDB12DFB71B45C99FE39E0A01F1D255.description: Wink, wiggle their ears, and other facial “tricks.”

322FB068AB2C4C3C877E29D80D910E33.description: Say more complex sounds (e.g., alveolar sounds – t, d, n).

6929A7F138B148A88196686B8B1A4473.description:
Say most sounds correctly. (l, s, r, v, z, ch, sh, and th may still be
challenging.)

A7E2933AD7F74B42BE65C6D9CF77A830.description:
Make different faces when a familiar adult asks them “What does mad/sad/
happy/etc. look like?”

69A74E798BD946DC851ABC350E85A4E1.description: Try to roll their tongue after seeing someone else do it.

98D1BFC622E84F0BB9DDF482C18A6ED2.description: “Blow” their nose when a familiar adult holds a tissue (both nostrils at once).

D46B0C0C13F14D8E8A5092A8D31AEF74.description:
Make happy, sad, angry, and surprised faces while looking at themselves in
a mirror.

3AED99DD201744F485480FA75666ADD9.description: Use a straw to blow a feather across the table.

701133E3AE864E319BA1892B1190FC0E.description: Explore and develop more precise control over the movements of their tongue and facial muscles.

A18F06C2AFB14D7EB4ADFB9D2C54A07B.description: Children explore and begin to develop skill in using their small muscles.

7B364F909DFB4EA7B59E448FAE9876E1.description: Balance while sitting on a yoga ball.

073E7C6ADC4641F88CF9BF1E051EB0AB.description: Run across the playground without falling.

64484BCA1FE74C9FB5903F0F907AA3F1.description: Climb on a short rock wall.

E6F4950D093E4EF59FFA37D40CCC20AD.description: Roll themselves up a ramp in their wheelchair.

8DACD4B16ACB4C78B0FE131C7957BBDC.description:
Use their large muscles for stationary and traveling movements, such as sitting upright, walking,
climbing, rolling a wheelchair or walker, etc.

7F6D7DF7F66341A39351EB42226E61B1.description: Skip with coordination and alternating foot and arm movements.

5B54BA270F194490AA5E2F03DA5C5EE3.description: Dribble a soccer ball with their feet.

2D4641FC125149DFBBEB804ECD192258.description: Tap a pattern with rhythm sticks.

952634F5BB334FB79705DE160A91FAA4.description: Follow the directions in a movement song.

3230E432D88E478DAEC05FE92721D4E1.description: Toss a ball to another child with more accuracy.

021CD9EE4B984B8ABDE6635CA855A508.description: Move through a simple obstacle course.

EFD21C0728154DAB887EA4D9679C2D20.description: Shake and turn a parachute to the directions in a song.

9E0F7CD90DB54B04A9D63FE27EBF579E.description: Practice kicking a ball into a net from varying distances.

E723F17162A146C7A28937BC04C22BDD.description:
Explore and develop more precise control over their large muscle movements, including moving
in rhythmic patterns as well as using their muscles to move objects in their environment with increasing
coordination.

EF32E85810494D98B307AABD2287BE8F.description: Move all the way across a set of monkey bars.

23B097B7ACA04B728C78981A54581A25.description:
Practice to increase the number of times they can dribble a basketball or
soccer ball.

D53CFF4EEC0E4B7C8D6D7D322F607B18.description: Measure the distance they jump and try to jump farther.

B4C096FE8D8A4A179E984A9C96DF2C32.description: Begin to move across the monkey bars.

AFD10FC00310413D9377E53476329B36.description: Throw a ball farther than before.

C29A42BA7A164F8890A03187C08DFCAD.description: Pedal a bike faster after using it every day during recess.

C81CEC63D9274A0D8EDADA865A554B55.description: Pedal a tricycle as fast as they can.

38B2301F72244443BE30507A2E6399FA.description: Climb on large motor equipment faster and with more confidence.

B2ADDB60B687408AAE74AC1D93A2E68C.description: Develop strength and stamina in their large muscles through repeated use.

3850CF6031A4412E8944F5500B834734.description: Children explore and begin to develop skill in using their large muscles.

C10F6B906B914E7CBEB07AE6FE0578C5.description: Ask a friend for help tying their shoes.

D126F9B49ED740BEB15C102E9135357E.description: High-five a classmate after racing them.

8EBE35BBC7694F90843401315F70C111.description: Show a classmate how to pedal a bike.

E2AE46174CF245C1B563EE3E4B7953EE.description: Help a classmate zip their coat.

AD18768B803E46B5837CB729BA96DBD1.description: Help a friend on the swing by pushing their back.

17BADBDBD1734075AA8B6C520E94A810.description: Work with another child to stack blocks into a tower.

8C04D3E6801043249483DBA65C374362.description: Help another child find their sleeve when putting on their coat.

C93CF68012D141589B30A1B3E9A399DB.description: Recognize and show respect for the varying physical skills and abilities of themselves and others.

ABC4EBB865904BA084B919FE57212BD3.description:
Develop their own challenges, such as putting bean bags on a balance
beam and avoiding the bean bags when crossing the balance beam.

45AF0EE72EAB4B8ABF19B641DE89B6E9.description:
Ask a familiar adult how long it takes to run around the playground and then
try to beat that time.

F58BF2967BD0409EA4F395902069EB5F.description: Ride a bike without training wheels.

478A606AABAD44FBABFB4518230C2F19.description: Try to climb monkey bars independently.

354166EE32FA45EAA64B8820E68DC2AE.description: Climb to a higher spot on a climbing wall.

3DA1B2C16C714BFF8495BC793DA84368.description: Ride a bike with training wheels.

0FB9C7D53FF44632BABEC3A940AC7D13.description: Ride a balance bike or scooter.

1F5559A330134A0F8A86C4DEF9C9E6B6.description: Try to walk the length of a balance beam or curb, over and over.

5BFAA59722804A3AB2AA4E0FC6C19E04.description: Explore and stretch the boundaries of their current physical abilities.

8377F3806B9E46F6A0F36092AF0E8E11.description: Copy dance moves from another person or from a video.

7A054083AED64F5C979E45F4B28CC1D3.description:
March in place while touching their right elbow to their left knee as it rises,
and their left elbow to their right knee when it comes up.

E6869ABE73454B4F85E1BE6583848CA6.description: Begin to show preference for a dominant hand (left/right handedness).

8D284E89E49F4D248DB8AACCFE619DFA.description: Reach across their body to pick up a crayon.

A178536BBBF04693A21FD55560B1573B.description:
Use both hands to touch their body parts during “Heads Shoulders Knees
and Toes.”

91ADD8BA1F3844D0BAA168F2B883AA23.description: Coordinate movements across and on both sides of the body.

161264342CC84DAEA099C6749C96AC1D.description: Move through an obstacle course, most of the time.

3701AD65C36F4319BBCB77970763E98E.description: Duck their head when walking under the slide.

F741889343FC4BBFBDDFE0CFC990DFF2.description:
Adjust their speed and strength when throwing a ball at targets that are
closer or farther away.

CBFE46064EFC4AA19AA52758306A6930.description: Dodge around other children when running, most of the time.

57004D9ED71A4C8486710CA51AD91892.description:
Explore how their bodies fit into different spaces, such as whether a tunnel
is too small for their shoulders to fit through or if their body will fit into a
cardboard box.

2D8C4DFD35F0448895B5B6DBE47A1B8C.description: Stretch out on the floor to compare their height to another child’s height.

8EA1524E866748559F446A030137F416.description: Toss or roll a ball to another child with increasing accuracy.

C98A799D789B457B90880458F918C7A1.description: Use distance vocabulary, such as near and far.

AE851E8CED0D4F249952D3F5B958D403.description: Move through a simple obstacle course without knocking things over.

B2BAB4C5ADD342DABAB4776C27CE2D1A.description: Notice that they have grown taller than a toy slide they used to play on.

38B1D03CF2C648DEBCAB82D689998E7C.description:
Explore and begin to perceive depth, distance, size, and the relationship between their own body
and the space around them.

CF126E40BC8943EF996CAC2F460AD363.description:
Demonstrates to a peer how to do the pinch and zoom gestures with their
finger and thumb on an iPad.

4E9FA552D16C48D9AC422A0C05B8D4F4.description: Use the correct body parts when dancing to “The Hokey Pokey.”

848FC08B3CF34215AFFDEF3677420AEE.description:
Hold up the correct number of fingers when a familiar adult says, “Show me
5 fingers!”

2B2EB8CA8A894133B3612F183F9F384E.description: Wrap a pipe cleaner around their finger to make it spiral.

F11E6FDA4FA64CFAA66DF2FD6CA11CB2.description: Identify their pinky finger while giving a “pinky promise.”

28F4FC599F844204A36464AAF9E5ACF6.description:
