Point to the correct body parts when dancing to “Head Shoulders Knees and
Toes.”

B19BB5BDAFA441D596FCB055C2BB8A46.description: Use their head and elbows while playing soccer.

FBB03C08C7334B7399089E6063FEFB35.description: Use their foot to open a garbage can with a foot lever.

B25ADD35D80F4CCEA923BE6BBE070BF0.description: Recognize parts of the human body and how their body helps them engage with their environment.

72123AFDD3E143A0B91C0A275A116990.description:
Participate in a group activity to create a book with lists and/or illustrations of
ways they used each of their senses that day.

C3FAC703200947188A4A5071157680BB.description:
Describe and sort foods based on their senses, such as sorting foods by
color or by texture.

34AD852E1FDF491AA52BD61797A4BF27.description:
Close their eyes and identify different animal noises being played through a
speaker.

DED53D264CCD4EB29632C729710CB971.description: Taste different foods and decide if they like them or not.

3C8D32671CE9441C879EC337E78DD2DD.description: Smell food being delivered for lunch and say, “That smells like chicken!”

3EC252B0116E4715B787AD527020CA1F.description: Identify smells (like spices or familiar smells) from smelling jars.

9F040C3BF464437EB39AF7ABA85E5E5C.description: Feel a bump on their arm and tell a familiar adult it is itchy.

4CC64BFAD7534B01A0392FF9D01FCB3D.description: Take a drink of milk and recognize that it tastes bad and tell a familiar adult.

D1E8C9A3FB234019836D1B72F4B2F792.description: Smell smoke from a bonfire outside and tell a familiar adult about it.

CFE528E142D44FBFA014DD3227FB9698.description:
Use their senses (hearing, vision, taste, touch, smell) and their voices to perceive and respond to
the world around them.

1449867885FD4557BC5221886B63D3A3.description: Children begin to understand their bodies and how they function.

standardSets.title: Communication, Language, and Early Literacy Development: 3-5 Years
standardSets.subject: Early Childhood Standards of Quality (2022-)

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

82EC5C5C27FC43EBB816E995A300BF3D.description: Begin to look over and modify their own writings and drawings.

7AE843814BF54AA392694656A94814AD.description: Begin to write words/letters representing words with spaces in between.

5D16BE76CF1C4689AC50692B4C88D85A.description: Write their name on drawings, dictation, and other works.

15AAF79135604223874919E1E7DFE536.description: Ask a familiar adult how to spell a word.

B7EE7A3BD1F04D77BECEC468725C63A7.description: Write words and stories using known words and invented spelling.

4372ED1FBB44413A91366C831003559A.description:
Begin to modify and add detail to their writing and drawings with prompting
and support.

62D6E30E9AFF40C4B201C724F5B872E2.description: Express their thoughts and feelings in text, writing letters and letter approximations as well as known words and invented spellings.

019111B121C94C6EA5F734088B380B5D.description: Use known letters and letter approximations to represent written words.

2BDB5FE75C9A4E3AB22F711AFC6B3566.description: Write some letters of the alphabet.

1F99CD4E7A93463BB122A3AC0FBA2FD4.description:
Print the letters in their own name in the correct order, most of the time, such
as when “signing in” to the learning environment.

FDC484D34E2C433B9E0590D2FB176327.description: Make marks on paper that are meant to represent letters.

951B6D9982A44917A5048122030A0DCA.description:
Make repeated marks on paper to represent lines and circles, with these
shapes growing clearer with experience over time.

18B6AC5A230C4D3BBA0ABB6319E9C2E4.description:
Show interest in using a variety of forms of early writing to convey meaning and represent sounds
and words.

D372D769B4884A619F199D2B91D1DCA6.description:
Use real and invented spelling to write notes and letters to familiar adults,
other children, and family members.

75BFBEDCFD524AEB9C0F742E6FCE03D4.description: Write text under a picture to describe the picture or tell a story.

05250E3240C44814924DBBB1822DCA0A.description: Draw pictures and write words to express their thoughts and ideas.

C4D41509FB20484FAF8A5F9CD0EE3C56.description: Use a tablet or computer to make words or write “stories.”

7431882BE05D46EA9055C577484D97A8.description:
Record their thoughts and ideas in a journal, including drawings, scribbles,
and invented spelling (or some combination of those).

B624B2D3B2CA4251BA5D7F60924280F4.description:
Write a note or story with drawings, letter approximations, and invented
spelling, and then ask a familiar adult to read it.

B21D40510D374EB195C42A46E27ED219.description: Explain the intended meaning of their writing and drawings.

E3E77E3CD1AD4F629357ED475D97E822.description:
Use invented spelling, drawings, and letter approximations to write a letter to
a friend or family member, sometimes.

0830AE5652CE4CF49E6E960D6AE1864E.description: Write a shopping list, menu, or party invitation during imaginative play.

0E3F1A8B27F140D08DDD28E441B4EDB4.description:
Print the letters in their own name from left to right, such as to “sign in” to the
learning environment.

6FDA1FB978FD43869A4955B9771CEB6A.description: Mimic the writing actions of familiar adults.

000D633A0F4E4C6284C68D7B4ECD51D7.description: Draw and scribble to represent a thought or something they’ve seen.

06AC3458FD334FBD8F24715A6578B716.description: Explain what their drawings or paintings represent.

9011655CAF3B48C7A3DE37DE3CD5E0C2.description: Ask a familiar adult what they are writing.

9997AF584D3444F798B3688B7D4D38B6.description: Develop an understanding that writing is a way of communicating for a variety of purposes.

03F208C70E464F4D8B462133F039E217.description: Use a tablet or computer to make words or write “stories.”

637D073B1A7A40F2894973313E947F5B.description:
Record their thoughts and ideas in a journal, including drawings, scribbles,
and invented spelling (or some combination of those).

ED605C0920EA428F8E5D176F75BA02D7.description: Practice making letters or words with a tablet or computer.

DDAA2419A91C4F8EA1CFCB7D5F9004D6.description: Use a variety of writing tools, such as pens, pencils, markers, colored pencils, etc.

9CCF58482E13489BA23798BF59F7DED5.description: Practice writing letter shapes in sand.

972D792361DF411A9098688353FD8F9E.description: Draw shapes, lines, and letters with their fingers in fingerpaint.

A1E8BD96899C40BBB2A5DC0DD4D25407.description: Attempt to draw letter shapes on paper with crayons or pencils.

DB3E7C7AE5354EBD8BE37FB3C3A31DE7.description: With guidance and support, explore a variety of writing tools and materials.

3B7E2E24A6584F599EDC6257FDCA0FD0.description:
Coordinate their movements with greater ease for complex tasks, such as
buttoning or cutting along a line.

DAC07B6799BF461FB54F3602E252C824.description:
Use a three-finger grasp (tripod grasp) with increasing confidence and ease
when holding drawing/writing tools.

7EF3E49C4D3B493392C79FAC8DD34F61.description:
Use a dominant hand for using paintbrushes, scissors, crayons, and other
tools.

6B6A058EEBF74F268C89D022DC3E75EE.description:
Begin to use a three-finger grasp (tripod grasp) when holding a pencil,
crayon, or other drawing/writing tools.

3FF1A326FE3047198B49AD0079616BAD.description: Draw letter-like forms with increasing accuracy and control.

A0D9DF58DE8244E9ACADC6351696CC2D.description:
Use scissors to cut along a line or cut out shapes on paper, with some
precision.

4AB9F37C92EA4A61ABCC8AA361887B38.description: Demonstrate limited precision and control in more complex fine motor tasks.

400CCC9FA1DF4A5787B5EFDEADF052FA.description: Make snips in paper with scissors.

3A086594BE8F41A481D64F0373278408.description:
Make repeated marks on paper to represent lines and circles, with these
shapes growing clearer with experience over time.

730D300D79734239B28E7036396FF917.description:
Draw or scribble to represent something they’ve seen or to convey a
thought.

1B08314255954BD992FB2259F1F0847F.description: Grasp writing tools with their thumb and fingers (pincer grasp).

81CF15DA9C6445DA8F034C833726A584.description:
Manipulate objects with hand-eye coordination, such as threading beads
with large holes onto thick string.

D8EA2AC3989C479E8C17F8436CB07CFB.description: Develop increasing control, strength, and coordination of small muscle groups.

5FF7904E7D4E4FE5A616B056F01A4D06.description: Children will demonstrate emerging understanding of writing as a way to communicate.

3565CFCBB1E34889A51BC27F30F9A910.description:
Actively participate in a story being read aloud by repeating or filling in
sounds, words, or actions throughout the story.

4B6E059F3F6146678BD0EE6B1D769391.description:
Learn and remember new information from the books they read or have
read to them, such as telling others that a platypus uses its nose to dig after
reading What Do You Do with a Tail Like This?

35CD234F62EB45D5B2F3D842238F6955.description:
Notice similarities between themselves and the characters in a story, or
between their own lives and what is happening in a story, such as saying “I
like lima beans too,” when reading A Bad Case of Stripes.

0BF79DB19E10464B9B1621328616A8C6.description: Identify the characters in a story.

C50255AB8CE9436697D693FB2B726A5A.description: Use flannel board pieces to retell a story.

A4143F31E9DA4CB99C6B6FDF6B3E42FC.description:
Use what they know about the characters and events of the story to make
predictions about what might come next.

A4271382B0404AA8BCFCBBEE9E26602A.description:
Ask and answer subjective or abstract questions about a story, such as
“How do you think the main character should solve their problem?” or “How
is the main character feeling? Why do you think they are feeling that way?”

837FD5665AC8475CB22496DB8568EE24.description:
Summarize a story, mentioning several key events or ideas and how they
connect the structure of the story.

934712414E04438AB21DB6BB18649BCA.description:
Identify the characters and main events of a story, as well as where the story
happens.

CEAAF36229244BCEA0AE7FC5D5688FCE.description:
Look at a picture and, with support and prompting, make up a story about
what is happening.

279910DAF1AA420B8948F3B258C43093.description:
Look at the pictures in an unfamiliar book to help them predict what might
happen next.

9AF556475371455E8766CF8A2A250701.description:
Show empathy for the characters in a story, such as worrying about Grover
in There’s a Monster at the End of this Book or saying that they are happy
when Max comes home to his family at the end of Where the Wild Things
Are.

D6DED419F3ED4C7994A43461C1260952.description:
Talk about possible consequences of a character’s actions, such as noticing
that the tree is bending in Chicka Chicka Boom Boom and wondering if the
letters will fall.

F5A09E709BB84F60B2FA4A499265B223.description:
Notice similarities to their own lives when being read a story, such as telling
another child that they made a snow angel yesterday when a familiar adult
reads about Peter making a snow angel in The Snowy Day.

FCBB12787D1F438A9DFA2CB5DB6E65FB.description:
Ask and answer factual questions about a text or story, such as “What was
the main character’s name” or “What comes next?”

19E95C4D52C241E392951019946AD728.description: Begin to run their fingers along the text in a book.

FFE628693F7641F2BAE8254419421966.description:
Begin to understand that the text on a page is separate or different from the
pictures.

540273A467F642C8939675BD3341DB5A.description:
Look at the pictures in a book when asked to describe what’s happening in
the story.

BA40B0FC20DB465994089F49AB28C58D.description:
Remember what will happen next when a familiar adult is reading a favorite
story aloud—for example, that the letters will fall out of the coconut tree at
the end of Chicka Chicka Boom Boom.

DABFA50D49A445DA88188F1138FDFE34.description:
Respond to silly, unrealistic situations in stories by laughing or expressing
disbelief, such as when the pigeon begs to drive the bus in Don’t Let the
Pigeon Drive the Bus!

B0EE0509F90E4D41911CD80692E8DEC9.description:
Remember events from earlier in a story, such as that the narrator of Green
Eggs and Ham does not like them in a house or with a mouse.

7F969EBF139B403DB26662B85F561EC4.description:
Answer a simple question about a story, such as “What is the cat wearing?”
“Boots!”

1BDB4C7F8AA448379558D2B8F64A1349.description: With support and prompting, describe what is happening in a picture.

628C5A10CBDE4314830402F2DD0B48D2.description:
Ask questions about what is being shown or happening in a particular picture
in a book.

79C08980D7394B4E8320D95A91203C2F.description:
Follow the text of a story left to right and top to bottom (if their home
language is English).

7864345757054307A59B2F5139799D39.description: Identify the parts of a book (front and back covers, title, author).

A1D02ACD7BAE494C8378BF86EF324A36.description: Follow the pages of a book left to right (if their home language is English).

BF8C3ECB290B41ABA9B9D970E3A48C22.description: Hold a book right-side up and with the front cover facing them.

37E718BF5F534B568C96890A722DD793.description: Pretend to read a book to a friend, stuffed animal, or pet.

C96B0CDAF8544060BDC2E00787F2FEBD.description: Use some language from a story when attempting to retell a story, such as saying “Chicka chicka boom!” as they turn pages in Chicka Boom Boom.

25B088D1D7C04AD39E1A46E872A404CC.description: Demonstrate reading-like behaviors with familiar text or print materials.

E0875991E68A4CB0BA692BA79D73B8EA.description: Children will interact with people and materials to increase their understanding of text.

3F409D45EC984AF8BC24F454E293D2E1.description: Identify the beginning and ending sound in words.

19E14A985AB34D02AD4C253DD1D5F515.description: With adult support, clap out the syllables of a word.

80FCCD6E30414D649FAB389A2FF43F93.description: Produce a series of rhyming words.

356CB4C7E232471980F31A0FBE64037E.description: When asked, identify whether two words start with the same sound.

C4E0C3EE5F7F407FBCA3C5CED87BC6DD.description:
Begin to recognize and identify separate syllables in words, such as in their
own name. For example: “A—ri—sa.”

2BACBEC6C38A441AB634BEE89FF40FE4.description: Identify the parts of compound words, such as book—shelf and race—car.

F7827BFE7C2F4F5986552C81C4CFA31B.description: Tell an adult that “here” and “cheer” rhyme but “here” and “there” do not.

5756700F28004D34B8F422F0E61906F8.description: Imitate and show enjoyment for rhymes and alliteration.

13317EF29CD44FDD905F0BA4EB82755D.description:
With adult support, identify when two words rhyme or begin with the same
sound.

B4889826518C4392A1127697CB5336FE.description: Recognize, manipulate, and play with sounds within words.

AF661EB456294BB99AB8CF7583464D46.description: Create and extend series of rhyming words.

6B517988CCEE4FA986A0C42CFCA795B3.description: Recognize final sounds in familiar words.

4BF10340CA29410082A43AE914594BC4.description: Recognize beginning sounds in familiar words.

3E8BCC24419A48BE9766C1BB935A49A1.description:
Recognize the difference between similar sounding words, such as blue and
glue.

3BCCE2FBED9446DF92EC9503391D431F.description: Identify rhymes in familiar words, games, stories, songs, and poems.

5621E146F61E4607925DFB0C7B359CF7.description: Recognize words that have matching sounds.

88A6FAC6F4BD43B8A87FBD553E66123E.description: Clap out the words in a song or sentence, with adult support.

AC13400064AC4780B9E4D0F89B5BDAD3.description: Say the last word of a repeating phrase in a familiar chant, song, or story.

F9FDFA30F1D44D8D86DC43691940659C.description:
Recognize some rhyming words, or words that sound the same, such as zip
and clip.

CB87B572A76A49DBB443DEA9F2E8B700.description: Act out the motions to familiar songs, chants, and fingerplays.

857046C0A73242E0B3A65B6AB82CB54A.description:
Notice and identify that some words start with the same sound, such as “cat
and cow start with kkkkk.”

49FFFDC3DE124431962D00C65CA626DD.description: Notice, manipulate, and play with the sounds of language.

8999526A12F145DC96CC520FCC0184AC.description:
Children will build their awareness of, and ability to work with, the sounds of
language.

4C9201DC0D8E49ABAC5392D61212A222.description:
Use invented spelling as they sound out new words, with and without adult
support.

500155B81A464B94ACC6108B2C6AF41A.description: Identify letters based on hearing their associated letter sounds.

B5D5B33F9EBE4BB0903B87F09CD91EF0.description:
Produce the letter sounds associated with the letters in their own name, with
adult support.

4E6B130EFBDF4C8A9CABE52690B3628F.description:
Make the letter sound associated with the first letter of a word, with adult
prompting.

E2BD45573D8E4F20A241E3EFD2F0BD15.description: Make the sounds associated with many of the letters they recognize.

4D58D8ED29D84C9D8B871313C202481E.description: Recognize the sounds associated with letters.

07A8502ADB8C44DE8898E4F083545421.description: Differentiate between uppercase and lowercase letters.

11BBA38C58B944DD8F360330423BEA5A.description:
Recognize and identify at least 18 uppercase and 15 lowercase letters by
the end of their prekindergarten year.

F693E46DF8484D7B8BC8183F4B61BDB6.description:
Recognize the printed form of their own name and other names of familiar
people (classmates, family members, etc.).

751E212A85374140B4A5EECFA18F5F34.description: Recognize and identify many uppercase and lowercase letters.

168DCF0F334D4C95A824CEC64F048574.description:
Recognize and identify the letters in their name when they appear in other
printed words.

BF0236F3113647C195CC7CF934B156B5.description:
Sort and/or match letter shapes, without necessarily being able to name or
identify those letters.

FB44BB8E3A7845BFBE5B64B54CD57149.description:
Notice a letter appearing in printed words as being the first letter of their
name.

BEB6212BD9E94152A9BA939B002BE1D2.description: Identify some frequently appearing letters and numbers.

FA775BE6DB914EFB8D37E9DE632611F0.description:
Recognize letters, the names of letters, and how the letters are shaped, as well as some personally
meaningful words.

21912E214D1F47A0A38690BF2F0BB9B7.description:
Children begin to understand that (in alphabetic languages like English) letters and
letter sounds represent the sounds of the spoken language.

7EECB1B144604FE7AB7D985D8C241B2C.description:
Use a device to record video of a gymnastics meet they attended and play it
back later when telling others about the experience.

6C641331F6A44E0CA506C4B067AB4868.description: Draw a picture of and write about the elephant they saw at the zoo.

9E16F8D3943B40C59A4D3CC5E71430CD.description:
Express their thoughts, experiences, and ideas using a variety of strategies,
including gestures and facial expressions, words, signs, pictures, text,
numerals, sounds, shapes, models, and photographs.

5C662E24B0D542AF8BA7F99D4B9525D0.description: Point to and talk about words and pictures in a variety of texts.

DFB5FDFBE96748AAB6D78194F7A2380B.description:
Finish the ends of repeating phrases or complete a rhyme or sentence
while an adult reads a book, such as “He ate through one apple, but he was
still....” “Hungry!”

D93FC7F1A70A45B8A47B725FBF624F6D.description: With support and prompting, describe what is happening in a picture.

AD65985E29F248B985245BA51FD637B2.description:
Use some language from a story when attempting to retell a story, such as
saying “Boom boom!” as they turn pages in Chicka Chicka Boom Boom.

241412EE9BC74D49A2031E675205263F.description:
Understand that print and pictures communicate ideas that can be read/viewed and understood
by others.

41AB855B3C4144D18A84E4B3BFD2CBF4.description:
Point to individual, sequential words on a page as they read (or attempt to read) each
word.

1DABC5D515474291B30CF6685DAD66B4.description: Track text from left to right, top to bottom, and page to page.

4B89BC4BA4C6432997CBED7AAB5F018B.description:
Recognize and show interest in the ways people use print, such as reading a story
about getting letters in the mail and then asking a familiar adult to send them a letter in
the mail or making and “reading” a grocery list during pretend play.

9DBC140FE9B947B7ADE205ED8F922AA9.description:
Begin to recognize the difference between letters, words, and sentences, such as
pointing out the word that starts with a particular letter.

958DB15901E04412862165930D02A3B4.description: Mimic and repeat familiar story routines, such as saying “the end” at the end of a book.

C29D01CF03F6448D9EC6375B51B93C4F.description: Begin to run their fingers along the text in a book.

0ECD5EA3E1A5401592678659A53F7884.description: Join in with adults saying “the end” at the end of a book.

9AFE97E2873F4576B4729BEE705091F4.description: Begin to understand that the text on a page is separate or different from the pictures.

47616B9381FF4019A92BE46341A57A59.description:
Begin to use pictures and logos in environmental print to attempt to decode the text,
such as a new label in the learning environment with a picture of a Crayola crayon
box to identify the basket of crayons, a picture of a STOP sign to wait at the end of a
hallway, or the red and white bullseye image to identify a Target store.

95C4F1AEA3A6475DB26AA69411D5B70C.description: Expand their environmental print vocabulary with some less familiar signs and logos.

F937F6480D8743A2A680AAD4A46F7C71.description: Demonstrate an understanding of print concepts.

4BE9D31731D14F8EB0871B710346674A.description:
Hold books upright and with front cover facing them and turn individual
pages to read a story either using the text or the pictures, or a combination
of both.

5496D58840ED4C14A671DF9BDA348763.description:
Turn to the approximate part of the book and then turn pages to find specific
parts of a story in the book.

866A7E9F01074105850FF7C5CA7D69A7.description:
Ask about, identify, and distinguish between the roles authors and illustrators
play in making a book.

11A750DD1D1E485DB7DB3AFC5F80BFC4.description:
Identify the parts of a book: the front and back covers, top and bottom, and
title.

B3EA9193ED8146EF9355D075DC22E012.description: Hold books with two hands and turn the pages.

CD4567BF96464569B53A8FAFBC69B946.description: Choose familiar books to “read” to themselves or to a doll or stuffed animal.

3BB954A473F84898BF6214BD9EF49259.description: Demonstrate interest in and care for books, including book handling concepts.

8EDFC75A7DE34DF695B97BD8E01CEE09.description:
With support and reminders, apply their understanding of conversational
routines, such as turn-taking and maintaining eye contact, to a variety
of situations and types of conversations (with a familiar adult, a peer, an
unfamiliar adult, at home, etc.) with increasing consistency.

EEC3862073B34614A35B03B69E6693FF.description:
Initiate conversations and stay on topic during through multiple turn-taking
exchanges.

791CEBE0F14C40F3BAA8128A5B5BC124.description:
Engage in peer-to-peer conversations, listening and responding while
staying on topic.

45FE4B4C3BCA4D66B9F08624A4BBC12A.description: Stay on topic during peer-to-peer and group conversations.

729629FDE9144E5B8F3C3E9099588612.description:
With some support and reminders, apply their understanding of
conversational routines, such as turn-taking and maintaining eye contact,
to a variety of situations and types of conversations (with a familiar adult, a
peer, an unfamiliar adult, at home, etc.).

EFD46381263F49619AEEBF92BE06BDDF.description:
Adjust their language and tone when having a conversation with younger
children.

FF393757F47D4D028AA75D1861BB38FC.description:
Adjust their volume and tone depending on the context of their conversation,
such as speaking with a friend or an unfamiliar adult, having a conversation
in the learning environment or in a public library.

AD0121DFE167491BB1C942A8133604B6.description:
Use nonverbal cues during conversations according to their personal
cultural context, including physical proximity, maintaining eye contact, asking
questions, etc.

B6AAF3FE37024D2E9D306AD1B00BA3F2.description:
With modeling and support, begin to apply their understanding of
conversational routines, such as turn-taking and maintaining eye contact,
to a variety of situations and types of conversations (with a familiar adult, a
peer, an unfamiliar adult, at home, etc.).

CF81E8F5C1DE4823981BDF8FA19487E2.description:
Take turns in conversation by initiating and sustaining a simple back and
forth conversation.

5C6D4F556D964445AD372C7A494C8E73.description: Show attention to a person they are having a conversation with.

BA16AC28046F4F219F9AAAFF7D6A982F.description:
With modeling and support, use polite terms such as please, thank you, and
excuse me with increasing consistency.

B24B67B2E49E495484C338E5332054FB.description: Follow the social expectations of their personal cultural context when communicating with others.

AEDDD6ABD62946C9BF39396A11C64843.description:
Return to previous topics of conversation with new information “Remember, I
told you about the zoo? This is a picture of the tiger!”

2C8AE30C4C3D4D9C98F1C48D8FD2D98F.description: Engage in a wider variety of conversational topics.

3B1E131082DB48D38660308FC944F77D.description:
Extend conversations by asking questions and making comments related to
the topic.

8FADCBB69B2440F8A66563CC21597677.description: Retell a story or describe one of their own experiences in sequence.

724C7BACEDDC4DA082F1904645201DB0.description: Tell a story out loud for a familiar adult to write down.

7FAF0E24AFB34091BA49BB4A32655B0A.description:
Hold extended back-and-forth conversations by asking questions and
making comments related to the topic, sometimes.

D26E02C54937484582A9BD181C9EDF80.description: Begin to hold longer back-and-forth conversations.

DFF5879F0370408D93E3ADB14511293B.description: Initiate and respond to communication with others.

89A8CC75B71148379928F319AB45897E.description: Communicate with others for a variety of purposes.

36049CB63FE1487AAEB1113077BE82CB.description:
Children use social and conversational skills, beginning with their home language
and cultural values.

ED05FEF7F1034A0D8668CA764980BE76.description: Use sentence structures that are grammatically complex, most of the time.

00C5BB617DBA49C2B5750AE2FEC7C33F.description:
Combine words and phrases into increasingly complex sentences. For
example: “Teisha’s moms came today and read us a story and they took
turns doing different voices!”

A0E25CF709504F5E84FC3709CCA0B925.description: Tell increasingly detailed stories about their lives.

253E786C2B9846889323EB1202C04AD5.description:
Use sentence structures reflective of their home languages, such as
adding adjectives after nouns (rather than before nouns, as in English). For
example: “I have a shirt blue.”

B8AE490E8A36406EB2CCBFF235FF3F0F.description:
Combine words and phrases into increasingly complex sentences. (e.g.,
“She doesn’t like peas, but I do!”)

70D3F757E3504357B2677C86777E8BF0.description:
Use plurals as well as past and future tense verbs correctly when telling
stories, most of the time. For example: “We went to the zoo. We saw two
tigers and I got popcorn!”

D4BB39F6BC704A9DA32A876FEFF14B6A.description:
Tell stories about their experiences using past, present, and future tenses
and terms interchangeably (e.g., “yesterday we go to the zoo”).

1A93A336066F4370BAB5E725C1861FA7.description:
Combine simple words into sentences, using plurals, past tense, subjectverb agreement, and the possessive form (although often incorrectly). For
example: “Mommy goed work.”

EFDC07018C554093A95B9046B6103948.description: Communicate using increasingly complex grammar and sentence structure.

04ADA0E5DA814A9FAD373F41282721AA.description: Describe events that happened in the past with many details.

5AC066817E6640A68CD7B63C7AF332D9.description: Ask specific questions to understand and solve problems.

A1B4E0F1238641A8854E258AAE5953E1.description:
Demonstrate an increasingly complex and varied vocabulary of over 1000
words or signs.

91F959584FB9467886D812C7DD3494AC.description: Answer questions with detailed and more abstract signs, words, and ideas.

1222E46B92A84C67B3ADFD6204C719F6.description: Combine 5-8 words or signs together into complete thoughts or sentences.

ECFF959485E54ACE9328287614B3B419.description: Use questions to ask for things or gain information.

6E9978C1B92E4B6D92F73A99F608A259.description:
Use their growing vocabulary to express their needs and describe objects,
relationships between objects, emotions, and actions, including an
increasing number of details.

7C401BFDC7224D458BBB5B53D53CFF83.description:
Demonstrate a broad and increasing vocabulary of about 500 words or
signs.

3D69B2F5C6324BCEADE995FC55CFD609.description: Use phrases and sentences of 4-5 words or signs.

D597F7C487254F37AAE579E14BE82A39.description: Answer simple questions with words or signs.

E5E193541E854033BAF701C410A873A3.description: Use phrases and sentences of 2-3 words.

BD3D4DAFECE64157B925D135DAB43330.description:
Use an increasingly complex and varied vocabulary to express their needs
and describe objects, relationships between objects, emotions, and actions.

66DAD539BB4E4657B7EEDCF0BB0F7511.description: Communicate clearly, using increasingly detailed signs, words, phrases, and sentences.

5EB93EEDE9414B05BACE40F5F9C3C1C1.description:
Begin to use some polite gestures that are commonly used in their family
and community, such as bowing to indicate respect, lowering their gaze
when speaking to adults, or greeting a friend with a hug.

985F06BC375C4B8FB108B4BD6384126C.description:
Still mispronounce some words, especially new, unusual, or complex words,
such as “buhsghetti” for spaghetti.

789377177D8E48B2A259CD6F38C301F9.description: Communicate clearly enough to be understood by most people.

B2B556BEB17D4B8F93ADB86903401D37.description:
Communicate using increasingly understandable language, including sounds, gestures, signs,
words, and language expressed using assistive devices.

D11AAB0649224F10B02E936846611253.description:
Children use language to express themselves to others, beginning with their home
language.

4D0C6814FE12404493E7EA2F0B6986C4.description:
Follow increasingly detailed, multi-step instructions, such as “Please put
away your markers and put your picture in your cubby, then choose a book
and join us on the carpet.”

B0ED5F0D4B5D486584F92B2C41B966A1.description: Follow multi-step instructions, such as “Put away your markers, choose a book, and come join us on the carpet.”

A1AA8FA0F80C4CADBEA72A98C10492E7.description:
Respond to repeated signs, words, and phrases with gestures and body
movements.

04A9079E1E2B44D3B8CBD1CD819B5DAF.description:
Follow one- or two-step directions that involve familiar experiences or
objects, such as “Pick up the ball and roll it to me,” or “Choose a book and
come sit down.”

6B2800B580384AFCBABB024AE4D7F4B2.description:
Participate in a group conversation by communicating their own perspective
when asked, such as by explaining that the classroom hamster likes yogurt
treats during a discussion about making sure their pets have what they need
to be healthy and happy.

72A07C18893546FAA361A193C28E1012.description:
Retell or use picture cards to identify the major events in a story they just
listened to.

0821A874D16A482EA5E21A98654139CD.description:
Show attention during primarily receptive interactions, such as listening to a
book being read aloud, by nodding, gesturing, interrupting to ask a related
question, etc.

4FF10ABEC584494E8ED9230D8228C5D7.description:
Show attention during longer and more complex conversations, either
spoken or signed.

67373A92D2DC4E57BDB162F811E3325F.description: Actively listen to short presentations and remember some details.

90EA821178D3472E85009C34A35EE432.description:
Listen attentively to a peer or adult when it is that person’s turn to talk during
a conversation.

DA48AEBDA0044F44B97129BE686AAF8C.description:
Answer when asked questions such as “Why do you think your friend is
sad?” “What happened to the block tower when you bumped into it?” “Who
can you ask for help with that?” or “Where could we look to find the answer
to that question?”

536074A9D6AE4D6DB968C461B722498F.description:
Listen to a story about a boy in the rain and respond with reasons from the
story when asked “Why did the boy in the story have wet shoes?”

80FF173A3C644E7AB54A1CA616C9B6C0.description:
Answers questions or points to objects/people when asked questions such
as “Who do you want to play with?” “What colors will you use to color the
dinosaur?” “Where is your backpack?” or “What do you want to play with?”

5EB70ED2109744E3BE04F31E57771AA2.description:
Listen as a familiar adult describes an idea or clarifies the meaning of a
word.

48F66A842D674E9CAAE21F5E2A51B1CA.description:
Respond yes or no (or nodding/shaking their head) when asked “Do you
want to go outside?”

CEDE46D7198047C09562C42FA994B193.description:
Bring the box of dinosaurs to the carpet when a familiar adult tells them that
dinosaurs are one of the choices to play with.

7794E9FEBC2542C395417DC3D014FD87.description:
Pick out a book from the bookshelf and bring it to a familiar adult when
asked to choose the next story to read.

7630095F8BF44D78A571F5EEA9422019.description:
Participate in conversations by showing attention and acknowledging
comments or questions, either spoken or signed.

CAF7BD2877A746B6B888F7ECBEED56EA.description: Demonstrate understanding of increasingly complex language, including non-verbal cues.

E588A11B22534131A25AEF32DCB09DCA.description:
Children develop an understanding of language, beginning with their home language
or dialect.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

5A646869DDDD443AAA3B571CEFED332B.description:
Work with the weaving loom frequently because, “it’s
just like my Abuela’s.”

D8EC5B7A054542D288551AC519781C61.description:
Describe why they like to play with the egg shakers (or
another favorite instrument).

0167902A0F2C49D9BA8D4984070648D3.description: Tell a friend they like their drawing.

56E2F43F33F3426AA87184B6B4F306FF.description:
Tell about their preferences in colors and textures, such
as saying that they want to play with the green plastic
blocks and not the blue ones.

0CE988AA4B2549DE9B11093374DC1488.description:
Move and dance to describe their own feelings, or a feeling/
idea from a story.

8C1F3D48547B4DD2913E083425015D4C.description:
Show their thoughts, ideas, and feelings through multiple art
forms, such as combining drawing with writing to express an
idea or draw or paint symbols on a clay formation.

D03590E0B9B04B298A2B17672F7A642D.description: Create a book of pictures that tell a story.

279E7E7614AE49989A23949F251F7AA6.description:
Mimic the sound of a musical instrument with their voice,
such as making high-pitched noises to match a triangle, or
low thumping sounds to match a drum.

6E072AAEDA2B430BBC6FCB2E4B6748B8.description:
Move ribbons or scarves in time with the music when
dancing to a song that switches from fast to slow, or slow to
fast.

ADDB634ED9B54A2D97B98F646D4EB869.description:
Compare and identify the differences between a slow song
and a fast one, or a quiet song and an upbeat one.

F57B1441566443CE9C745AE8DAFDFD7A.description: Move their body in ways that match the mood of a song.

F6FA1734581C4FB491A28C2D6D83E930.description:
Draw a picture and describe or dictate to a familiar adult
what the picture is showing.

50BBA541482A4ED0BD95D111682B340B.description:
Use drawings (including scribbles) to tell a story or describe
a concept (such as showing who is part of their family).

ED4DA324DD29465C92815C59EBD5F36A.description: Sing a silly song and laugh.

9403671E4C4841D691C540981A5169A3.description:
Experiment with different instruments to match the sounds in
a song.

1D1FDC12227D4D0C884BEBD9F4635848.description:
Experiment with a variety of instruments and recognize their
differing sounds.

8B6EDB65387B4FFCAC4DA818430B7103.description:
Tap on a drum, a table, and a cardboard box to hear the
different sounds.

BD3F4389EBF3404C8F7DC19F4B70D361.description:
Explore different musical instruments, such as bells,
xylophones, and maracas.

BB86B509AC7348858795F1B6AE72D298.description:
Bang on a drum or pot to make loud noises and show
frustration—or delight.

99A5D4CA602549958B99D26041D24E20.description:
Point out the differences in color or mood (happy, sad)
between two pictures.

84942A69F9D148399D60A378DFD3CE45.description:
Explore, recognize, and respond to similarities and differences between works of art, and
the emotions, moods, situations, and cultures being expressed.

E420F06B0B564837AD8545EDBED1EFE6.description: Children develop preferences and appreciation for the arts.

D22A1B22828C4DC08C5FF87155A7A4C7.description:
Focus on a single work for longer periods of time, such as sessions over 30
minutes, returning later in the day, and/or working over multiple days.

D14CF49072BC4A6F9C981B106F8CF493.description: Add details to their work and revise when necessary.

0C9D38BC57004C4F90305DB30AC94EF3.description:
Plan a creation, saying, “I’m going to paint a picture of my cat. She has
brown stripes and a white belly.”

A03948C5C17A4B6B953970F25F50E60E.description: Use a variety of media (paint, text, music, etc.) to express themselves.

AF61FAD782524D7B9D512C2C496E9561.description:
Ask questions about a prompt to “Draw and write about your day” to clarify if it
should only be about school-time or if they can draw their morning routine too.

AD4B228FF98F497A86F5B551488BBDAA.description: Create intentional designs in their work.

FEDCDADEBD5F4B529ADCF4EA37ABA68A.description: When asked, describe their plan for a drawing or painting.

554BE7F641E34E9D8A2BBCDDED5F0925.description: With and without prompting, communicate their ideas through the arts.

1702527244654BA9B6F45DAB95D64DFD.description: Draw straight and curved lines to create pictures.

DB96AB0BFD9C45C9A1C8D2166949535F.description:
Follow along with appropriate body movements during “Head Shoulders
Knees and Toes.”

F5B62B11A8A340CB9EAB85E726B73949.description: With prompting, express their ideas through the arts.

DAA4E4E23B5243C98AE0E9E9B88A22F4.description: Plan and create works of art with increasing intentionality and detail.

B1688F94CEBF4B73A0FBD4F007807A87.description:
Experiment with changing the pressure they use on their crayons or colored
pencils to make dark and light shades.

42FEE3AD3DD346E491515DF78512C0DD.description: Combine two colors of paint to get the shade they want.

DFC329ABCA88417887DF3B19B1A3DDEE.description: Use terms like sculpture, sketch, and melody to describe art, sometimes.

AC8ADC403BEF491F9BD8CCB618E94B33.description:
Use creative tools with noticeable control as they create artwork with some
detail and intentional color choices.

6482B7EB00A440559B19CAC3C1F41C57.description: Match the beat of a song when playing an instrument along with music.

8699F80940B34208A7C21561AC237388.description: Use tissue paper, construction paper, and glitter glue to make a collage.

1CC79988A98D427BB4362FBAD598CF40.description:
Use whatever materials are on hand (blocks, paint, playdough,
manipulatives) to create something new.

F198A63B9E3F47BE9F957327A3368986.description:
Experiment with the angles they can hold a crayon or marker to make
different kinds of marks.

21AEF47EE2EE41CDBF53A4F3B2296CC1.description: Use cookie cutters and rollers to shape playdough.

B0A8B24831F743D3A74E05F6A198951A.description: Repeat part of a song they have just heard for the first time.

DC2A9E457C7741D6ACF54C3AC6B3C72A.description: Use terms like collage, rhythm, and watercolor to describe art, sometimes.

662F01EC099F48C9989A8AEE8222F61C.description: Point to a jar of paint or basket of crayons and ask to use them.

064900EFC72244D1AFDA551293AC3F6A.description: Use terms like volume, beat, and shadow to describe art, sometimes.

A944B4B8CE7D40BA86FD35B4F8B1761F.description:
With support, use tongue depressors to make bunny ears in a ball of
playdough.

11207BA2741349B58658D6F53BB2156E.description: Make different sounds with their voice (loud/soft, high/low).

4023BFBD8C4948A99F4A20D9B47E6ABE.description: Use props like ribbon sticks, scarves, and dolls while dancing to music.

4F83DA7ABE8A4BDB9F77F50B42FC8B60.description: Make “pizza” out of playdough and pretend to eat it during imaginative play.

1919B3A5B5D14DC18BE50ECA98B3380C.description: Use a towel as a blanket to “tuck in” a doll for bedtime.

C5919F5B480F4354A0BC04E228D154BB.description:
Explore, use, and begin to use artistic vocabulary to describe the tools, mediums, and components
of the arts.

BA0928ABB35044D3ACDD4207BD5C26A8.description:
Use fine motor skills to pinch, push, and form playdough into the shape they
want.

29FC42B4A624492DBD96F047F7824B75.description: Match the beat of a song when playing an instrument along with music.

3D10052C80DE4323824A135B3330429E.description:
Imitate a familiar adult’s movements when trying to learn a new dance, most
of the time.

5CDAB248FEA841039E3F487A09536A2C.description:
Show more control in making intentional marks, such as straight and curved
lines.

37C1670C915E4D1CA54A3B2D41E1883E.description:
Use scissors with more precision, cutting along dotted or folded lines, most
of the time.

9E8C403555174D0EB658D2200E982989.description: Draw and combine shapes into more complex figures.

2333A0A1B2684F8FB6E9457BA73C3258.description:
Match and repeat a rhythm demonstrated by a familiar adult, such as
stomping their feet back and forth (left-right, left-right) four times.

2D2870541DCE40389D66A28A478C4A5F.description: Dance to the (approximate) beat of different kinds of music, most of the time.

173E256ABBBA40FEA799C12AE23FEF52.description: Draw straight and curved lines to create pictures.

408FEF4342284FBDBBC645CCF20E10E9.description: Attempt to mimic a familiar adult’s clapping rhythm.

21484FCEC7B049D28C3FFB88249A5F85.description: Squish and roll playdough into balls and snakes.

D3D6ABE85D6646D3B8B03C8DEF0CF9DB.description:
Play along with songs like “Hokey Pokey” and “Head Shoulders Knees and
Toes.”

DB75BDF15CC74411A59C534E5107580F.description: Explore and develop increasing control over fine motor and large motor movements.

9F4F0F6496114C279F02D4ECFD56C247.description: Children develop the skills that support self-expression through a variety of art forms.

1BD9B4B713B04E7DA141300C95FA5673.description:
Work with other children to decide on the details of a story to tell in
their play, and who will perform each role.

3767C7ACA38F4CCEBF0197B4822AB2DB.description:
Act out familiar stories or characters from books, movies, or
television.

5D9F73AD657A4F6485615002BBA4388E.description:
Explain to other children their ideas or plans for play, such as
describing the roles they want each person to act out.

E2A90831E9EA4E318CBD892CE19527F5.description:
Mimic words and phrases commonly used by familiar adults or
favorite shows.

7DAC0B02259E492490BAD56DB9450D23.description:
Join in cooperative pretend play with other children, passing
dishes around the table during a pretend meal.

0B03F87EBF4941CFAB3780740D05EA4F.description:
Imitate other people’s conversations and interactions during
pretend play, in a similar context to how they heard or experienced
the conversation initially. Often, they will recite memorable words
and phrases.

DF2D752DC6274F2A8539E19449F3557D.description:
Explore roles, express thoughts, and feelings, recreate experiences, and act out stories
through the arts.

47F9F0285CC84C4B90ABE28B95673B08.description:
Extend their pretend play with other children by including more themes,
detail, and storylines, such as turning a pretend meal into a Thanksgiving,
Chinese New Year, or Kwanzaa dinner with cousins, aunts, and uncles.

332114A1FC0847EBB8017FE14380AB2E.description:
Incorporate their home culture into color, texture, and musical choices in
their artwork.

E7EE6296790A46B3993FA3585E30203D.description:
Engage in a discussion with other children to decide which favorite foods
from home will be served during their pretend meal (collaborative pretend
play).

C882D39853EA45F9951F47AACA02513A.description: Show some preference for dolls that look like themselves.

CB2153EF1A344864AE61AA38BA45F827.description:
Wear “dress up” clothes that are similar to those commonly worn by their
family.

205FB7A01F9445CEA8C889103CA38897.description:
Explore and experiment with the arts through the lens of their personal cultural context and that of
others.

8FC1C8A99B964DE0BDA7D55C5D09EF9D.description:
Use fine motor skills to pinch, push, and form playdough into the shape they
want.

FF2C7B8D23B54C5DBFFD43C4EBB3463F.description:
Invent their own songs – sometimes just music and sometimes also with
lyrics.

4B38D8D915A4447FAEE8983D089EA26B.description: Contribute to group storytelling and songwriting.

1A49F92725134952A7D53A65A9D62772.description: Draw and combine shapes into more complex figures.

C8D16F63DFDD48AE83D96A1D0F6A3A89.description:
Respond with matching movements when asked to move like a certain
animal (arms out like a bird, hop like a kangaroo, etc.).

8D8EF71CD4B94777BC140666F3A85A66.description: Follow the directions in a movement song.

2856CA07FA8B402EBE2A929444C94455.description: Talk with others about the artwork they have made.

BDFEF1C3DA7949D49B8574FA6997FB29.description: Hum the tune of a familiar or invented song.

62C101757C6F406F847FD3E507A1A495.description:
Display their artwork to a familiar adult, and say, “Take a picture for my
daddy!”

4347E7C5265F4D51A36CAC3807BB0628.description: When prompted, describe what they are creating.

A0479C008435425489D5DF2A39FA2040.description:
Explore and experiment with the arts in increasingly creative ways to express themselves, with
modifications as needed.

1567D7E7933C466F8877E6C860687AE3.description:
Children develop healthy self-concepts through creative self-expression that draws from
their backgrounds, experiences, and identities.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

2C2C15DA47C94E5AA7D5803B700DBC3C.description: Collect leaves and sort by type of tree and/or leaf shapes.

8DA461416590432E994208A0DB8CAA3C.description: Sort manipulatives into separate containers during clean up time.

EEB90588188A4C138A9F9445324C84C7.description:
Organize buttons based on different attributes, such as solid color, stripes,
dots.

05FE2AAF658746B8B8B1129AF868C17F.description:
Sort animals by habitat (farm or forest, for example), when directed by an
adult.

3BC6A1A9BB3F4FE78E339AC5108EDA32.description:
Sort blocks by material (plastic/wooden) during clean-up time, when directed
by an adult.

883C846FE0744FF8A52FF1D2A07EE3C0.description: Sort things in their environment into groups based on attributes.

11C02FB3FDE948818D922DC65E087350.description:
Classify items by their similarities, such as “all of these animals have fur, and
these ones over here have scales!”

3827CC3CB231498B9D56CEA722D7B404.description: Measure the growth of their seedling every day.

ABB1B331C4A54F77945B7B5E7F35B123.description:
Chart different kinds of weather with their group over the course of a week or
a month.

10AB4302300942AFA260FCF2F55A7228.description:
Ask the other children if they have a cat at home and make marks in their
journal to count how many.

897741CF6BE2417E9C059686335782AF.description:
Describe the similarities and differences between objects, such as
determining by feel that some of a collection of buttons are fabric-covered
and others have holes.

62071A89EEC34FEC99E53DF26F22686E.description:
Participate in a group activity to count how many people in the group have
pets.

24E69C1228EC4824A1CCC14CAD1DA47B.description:
Begin to describe the difference between objects, such as telling that one
doll has a blue dress and the other has a red dress.

651942F95D7049E78319A113A153AD56.description: Recognize and classify things in their environment.

5C1D6FC1D19C48BB802BA184AB2CEAFB.description:
Children begin to develop processes and strategies for classifying
and using data.

E578B41BA81C4068896C1B8F141840A3.description: With support, measure ingredients for making bread.

6E4F5C1B353347339689BC95D5CA21A0.description:
Expand their use of formal measuring tools to include more complex or
detailed tools, such as rulers, kitchen and bathroom scales, thermometers,
etc.

D78E62C85DD84366AA6DD1243BEEFA9E.description:
Use informal measuring tools, such as footsteps, hands, or blocks to
measure length, volume, and other measurable characteristics.

34A2714F3D144921825AAAC80C4D3704.description:
Begin to use formal measuring tools, such as tape measures and balance
scales, to determine size and weight.

9F83CC50AC1549E5931A76E53F09039B.description: Hold a piece of fruit in each hand to decide which is heavier.

57AADA4BD15D4C43B5E236DE127F7F84.description:
Use a cup to move sand into a bucket, counting out loud as they pour each
cupful in, sometimes.

CCD32E468CB643C59973C04E77C28921.description: Use non-standard and standard tools and units of measurement.

976FCD75087444A3B414E1954BE00103.description:
Point out that one book must be “longer” than another one because the
spine is thicker.

6F6CFE23D644494AA675A0C74BAEA6EE.description:
Place blocks tightly against each other to compare the area, or space inside,
two differently sized rectangles, with more accuracy.

9FB55670C6A54449AF6119E95ABFBC05.description:
With prompting, place blocks somewhat randomly inside two differently sized
squares to compare how much space is inside each square (area), with
some accuracy.

1D860B1EB94045498908D73B01935641.description:
Set several blocks next to each other, using trial and error to decide which is
longest, when working to line blocks from longest to shortest.

E7B37A58FF844891A2C9A68FB8288FF9.description:
Compare size with simple terms, such as bigger, smaller, taller, shorter,
lighter, and heavier.

7961492CD0824167AC0CF6B9393813B5.description:
Compare things in their environment and use the language of measurement (lighter, darker, long,
longer, big, bigger, etc.) to describe them.

F43803E3D96F48EE8E45D480554C4831.description: Ask a familiar adult to help them measure string for a bracelet.

5ADEB1D4F7734043B96882DB50399CB6.description:
Participate in a group discussion to decide which shelf will best fit the
wooden unit blocks.

07CAF2C7F3A148BB89155405581FA094.description:
Draw scribbles and spirals both inside and outside the lines when asked to
“color in” or “fill in” a square (early recognition of area).

38B8158FCE5349C7B2C26DAF34F7902D.description:
Notice and recognize that things in their environment can be measured (length/height, weight, area,
volume, temperature, time).

D338575AE7F645ABB2BB4CDFB672BAC9.description: Children show a growing understanding of the concepts of quantifying and comparing.

7D49D808D29B4631AD340D04D6D00D95.description:
Use a mental map of ordering as they set stacking cups in a row from
smallest to largest.

283D585AA78044D8AD55EEF42443A793.description:
Place rods of Unifix cubes in order from shortest to longest based on the
number of individual cubes.

70AFDEC52E3F4E2F84D14910BAF037DF.description:
Set several blocks next to each other, using trial and error to decide which is
longest, when working to line blocks from longest to shortest.

D834BCC0408F4E45A46D1E6A78B97B58.description: Choose picture books from the library that have main characters who look like them.

ABAEFD8246B04CC39D4EAE3EFAAB12EC.description:
Ordering and Seriation: Arrange objects in order according to changes in a specific attribute, such
as size, length, number, color, etc.

FAC0B6CB87B143149F1FB4402258CD08.description:
Begin to copy patterns into other materials. For example: looking at an AAB
pattern made with yellow and blue counting bears, draw that pattern with
yellow and blue crayons.

2640B3895CD140CDA9E40D724494A979.description: Recognize, identify, and build repeating AAB and AABC patterns.

E652FBA9D6FE45A8978FDCC5EF1B8B6C.description: Recognize, identify, and build repeating AB and ABC patterns.

C4E8F87B420A40479FD3D86526998D25.description:
Continue a pattern set out by an adult, adding a triangle and then a circle to
a row of triangle, circle, triangle, circle.

E54820793D584DD09BE87C85B0B466D2.description:
While looking at a pattern of blocks set out by an adult, copy the pattern with
their own set of blocks.

7C82586D26764A6AB82E80E1D2DEBB8B.description:
Put a blue counting bear in the empty spot in a row of yellow bear, blue,
yellow, empty space, yellow.

F33443AC52D6477DA5083C1EFB842AF2.description:
Recognizing and Building Patterns: Notice, recognize, copy, extend, and create repeating
patterns.

78CD9CA57894428685B8201E990381B3.description:
Children show a growing understanding of patterns, structures, and relationships
in math.

CCCE1A07A0224678BE29060FA4BB3D22.description:
Quickly answer questions about the parts of a whole. For example,
recognizing that if there are 3 green blocks and 1 red block, there are 4
blocks, or if there are 6 candies then 3 people can share with 2 candies
each.

64DB9FF5ECAC476CAB1BD261C60ADD99.description:
Begin extending their understanding of equal parts to include 1/4 and 1/3,
such as 4 parts of a sandwich or separating crackers into 3 equal piles.

C4A224FB76974A45AA1AF0443CF9EB2F.description:
Begin to identify “half” of a circle (cookie) or square (sandwich), as well as
“half” of a countable quantity (crackers) as they apply to “fair shares.”

8923CE402C5E4190811303D0B950A1AF.description:
Continue to explore and become more accurate in dividing shapes into equal
parts.

73D78836206E4F54BB9E97E2B3A695F0.description:
Attempt to label a whole and its parts with numbers, such as explaining that
their basket of 4 pieces of play food has 2 pears and 2 oranges.

5B09FE6269E740A9AA35AD08DD2F686F.description:
Begin to use tools to divide playdough shapes (circle, square, or rectangle)
into two or more generally equal parts, through trial and error, and they may
not be able to explain how they decided what was “equal.”

FA09762E9E3B4420B327994DF81F3E24.description:
Recognize that parts make up a whole, and whole is bigger than individual
parts. However, they may not be able to use numbers or measurements to
explain why this is the case.

BE49C7FA405248EBB3285227D3164DE8.description:
Investigate and begin to understand the concept of a whole and how it can be divided into two (or
more) equal parts.

23F40ED39B934A1D80CC26417E7416E9.description:
Use blocks to build taller arches and enclosures/rooms, and begin to build bridges, ramps, stairs,
and add roofs to their constructions.

EA64688185B44181884CE197B32E71BD.description:
Draw a line on a simple illustration of a house to show the separation between a triangle and a
square (identifying and decomposing shapes).

00F1FE8EDE074D71874CBBD9369D8686.description:
Put together simple tangram or pattern block forms, creating new shapes. They may need to
follow a model or map.

16BA022828EF48A4ADD7066AF9D916F1.description:
Use more shapes to add complexity to their drawings, such as using 2 rectangles to form the
upper and lower arm in a drawing of a person.

96F74BE6341B4B1A940D4A71F0597025.description:
Recognize that the faces of 3-dimensional shapes are 2-dimensional shapes, such as identifying
the side of a cube/box as a square.

19583CD09A45415086B895B00BDF12F2.description:
Recognize and identify more complex shapes, such as the trapezoid, rhombus (diamond), and
hexagon, as well as more 3-dimensional shapes, beginning to learn the formal terms for these
shapes.

6B14BC9A4567424F89FD328F62902F87.description:
Recognize lines and angles (corners) as attributes of shapes when comparing and classifying
shapes. For example: noting that a triangle has 3 sides, but a rectangle has 4.

90D7FE8A29F34034B7146702B3E4F3E2.description:
Point out lines and angles as geometric objects, at least in the context of how they can be put
together to form shapes.

D28B6F301CE641998371DEBDA7AB4C25.description:
Begin to build arches and enclosures/rooms with interior space, with more understanding of what
shapes they will need and how to build it.

91E9DA6C66EF423FB4B03D8720BB1D97.description:
Use shapes as parts of their drawings, such as using a square as the body of a house and a
triangle as the roof.

775D57C1D57C4B858A517498FB8D5F65.description: Use blocks to create the lines of a shape, so their creation looks like a particular shape.

634115A4063B4A799177BDA916BBA4F5.description:
Recognize a wider variety of shapes, such as identifying a book cover as a rectangle, and a line
drawn across the angle/corner of a square as forming a triangle.

1D008D9C20774368A553141E5BFD712A.description: Continue to expand the range of shapes they can match, even with size or rotation differences.

4E27986B86274B1E8942EC42AB1E1178.description:
Begin to use blocks to build arches, corners, and enclosures or “rooms,” though the constructions
may not have interior space and may have been constructed through trial and error.

068D75ED84EE424EBB7239B8F6718B24.description: Begin to compare shapes using simple terms, such as being pointy or tall.

3C042D71103B4D17BAFCD6DA19DC702B.description: Identify circles and squares and begin to recognize and identify a sphere (ball) and a cube (box).

F82BC69F7BA8482CAB3D8888B1E4AE2D.description:
Turn two books to line up with each other, so they can check if they are the same shape,
sometimes.

15C7EC853E234A049DBF5B558ECEE880.description:
Match more shapes, such as rectangles, ovals, etc., even if they are different sizes or rotated
differently, such as pointing out two rectangular blocks as matches, even though one was
sideways and the other flat on the floor.

87078CC1F5584D61A308FCC495C8DC11.description: Explore and begin to analyze two-dimensional and three-dimensional shapes and shape attributes.

2E615C9B1B2A424B933F4F5F2B42CC89.description: Quickly decide if puzzle pieces will fit in the spot they are working on.

1F02A546065E4520B5B0275283AA1310.description: Walk around furniture and other people without bumping into them.

D65ACACEC7C04ABF9CEB2909DEE3FFAE.description: Move successfully through a simple obstacle course.

0EF552053050434C8EE076B24F47B786.description:
Label or name some locations during play, such as “That corner is home
base!”

022B644C053041C69163513B74081D40.description:
Keep track of themselves and where they’ve been as they move through a
maze.

A2F5D129E18A4BA29EB210C2A7BB90EC.description:
Begin to build a mental model of a line between dots on a graph to predict
where two “lines” might meet.

59CB0183B78243DDAE2ED46B392A3794.description: Recognize a taller bar in a bar graph means that bar has “more.”

060457878E084BBAA0C3D9C9867CAE79.description:
Continue to expand their spatial and directional vocabulary, including terms
such as left and right, as well as in front of and behind.

E3B41A540E9C49A7885DF2A750152A4F.description: Find a toy that has been misplaced or intentionally hidden.

14727ED4C93F40FF9711F193429D0D0E.description:
Look over puzzle pieces to narrow down the group to just those that might fit
in the space they are trying to fill, without using trial and error for each piece,
sometimes.

8F917F8922EB434F98D8858EA002F0D5.description:
Expand their spatial vocabulary to include more complex terms such as
beside and between.

D5E5FC6B8F764A1EB5C90F5D13ADA58C.description:
Explore and begin to recognize the positional relationships between objects, their environment, and
themselves.

40D4BECE90D4494DA2C50494DB67F157.description: Children show a growing understanding of shapes and spatial relationships.

CD643A7E04BF4EE6B8672ED115982907.description:
Quickly answer questions about the parts of a whole. For example,
recognizing that if there are 3 green blocks and 1 red block, there are 4
blocks, or if there are 6 candies then 3 people can share with 2 candies
each.

A7A00CCBC539481EB66BFE3406A24DE4.description:
Mentally separate larger groups of objects in two or more smaller groups
when figuring out quantity. For example, with a plate of 7 apple slices,
visually separate into groups of 3 and 4 to be able to easily decide there are
7 slices.

303EF46BFBC142A58C03B913DE78F574.description:
Recognizes and produces number combinations up to 4. For example,
moving a collection of four toy cars to groups of 1 and 3, 2 and 3, 3 and 1, 4
and 0.

2981A3E1442746A59CF1052ED0084394.description:
Attempt to label a whole and its parts with numbers, such as explaining that
their basket of 4 pieces of play food has 2 pears and 2 oranges.

C4ABEF78AFAD43EE90E5396C5DAFF732.description: Trade 2 small items for 1 bigger item.

FD149AF1ACDD4A4E9841F7ADA916E68B.description:
Recognize that parts make up a whole, and whole is bigger than individual
parts. However, they may not be able to use numbers or measurements to
explain why this is the case.

AAA48882D194447395C081AE9C9FB28A.description:
Composing and Decomposing Numbers: Begin to understand that numbers are made up of
smaller numbers.

6369B14C8DE24A2AA4B2E5687E405C77.description: Tell how many children are present after counting how many are absent.

8B330285ED714F3EB7EEC4EDF27AE42F.description:
Mentally separate larger groups of objects in two or more smaller groups
when figuring out quantity. For example, with a plate of 7 apple slices,
visually separate into groups of 3 and 4 to be able to easily decide there are
7 slices.

86EEC8FD05434446BF673DDAA308A4B9.description:
Use finger patterns, objects, and counting on to join quantities together. For
example, when prompted with “You have 7 cheese sticks, and someone
gives you 5 more. How many do you have now?” will start at 7 and counting
8, 9, 10, 11, 12 until they have counted 5 more numbers to find the sum.

8BF49CE24E484085A5829DA8517472FF.description:
After naming who is missing during the morning message, tell how many
children are absent today.

3801DDB46E594B6EA6F559A780AE4E2D.description: Tell how many children are present after counting how many are absent.

777275D5B869494FB4D2807DC31483D9.description: Say that William has more blocks than they do, after counting.

FF673BC1D3BA432F978078DEECAA38C9.description:
Look at the two pieces of crackers on their plate, compare that with the three
on Laura’s plate and say, “I need one more.”

284CA40E52EC4D50AD7502E30DC4B52F.description: Choose the biggest piece of cake.

927A168761D249F48067C5263013A2E9.description:
Tell who is first and who is second in a race or other scenario. For example,
“Sarah finished her snack first, and I finished second.”

26B9704A88A84E87B533AD852B8744A6.description:
Comparing, Adding, and Subtracting Numbers: Begin to understand numbers as sets to be
compared, put together, and taken apart.

9A1BA95F72DC496787A08F83AEA90E38.description:
Mentally separate a large group of objects into two or more smaller groups.
For example, recognizing that they have five blueberries, and their sister
also has five, so there are ten blueberries in all.

F55F569F99C24D0E8CABC95445FBB444.description:
Recognize some common number arrangements, such as 5 and 5 makes
10.

B3080B2EC0274367A6AFB821C9A782C2.description:
Demonstrate “conceptual subitizing,” or identifying a whole when only seeing
parts of it. For example, seeing five cookies stacked and overlapped on a
plate and saying that they see five.

3C9A7892C0254A0B8A4458A39A2BEA06.description:
Recognize that they have five counting bears, and their friend has four, so
they have more than their friend.

C1732C6BF36F4AB886E6D9A5442FC42E.description: Tell a familiar adult that there are “only two” Goldfish crackers on their plate after looking but not counting.

806AF4DCE39D433EA503F71179A1F366.description: Subitizing: Recognize and name the quantity of objects in a group without counting.

EA263C02E92E45CC89A1092B3CECE995.description:
Keep track of what they counted and what they haven’t counted in a group of
objects.

27223869EB15483FA2AB6F7FB0E428B1.description:
Show an understanding of cardinality, or the understanding that the last number
said when counting is the total quantity. For example: counting the cards in their
hand, and saying, “I have six cards.”

72934D5B87224F93B9DBE5027E890783.description: Pass out ten crackers for each child.

EED28EF0D0BB4D749DD99AAB13BAC1B4.description:
While pretending to launch a rocket, count backwards 5,4,3,2,1 and then shout,
“BLAST OFF!”

4953809C90B8424A845C3BE11987C647.description: Pass out one plate and one cup to each child.

AB3721DB2B6844D4A445A88DCD46EAC8.description: Roll a die that lands on 5, then move their game piece five spaces.

EA0B8C257EFB4450B667E55E87DB600A.description: Serve themselves five carrot sticks for snack.

C2471BCDCB9043BA96B4F0D71FFE7CC9.description: Point to animal counters one-by-one, counting out loud from one to five.

87E1065983934FD597253725AB9D0ADB.description:
Counting: Explore numbers and number vocabulary with increasing understanding of their
relationship to quantity.

D5B1385BF5B245FE9319A3913CA92156.description: Children show a growing understanding of the concept of number and quantity.

631E9AA7875E4BCD86A5B7E56A89E87A.description:
When their first idea for a solution doesn’t work, try to think of other ways to
solve their problem or achieve the result they want. For example: when the
mosaic tiles they chose for their city artwork are too heavy for the paper, tell
a familiar adult they might need to choose something else to work with, or
different paper, or maybe even different glue to make it stick better.

FD32A620863342F29E1C18FEF31790A5.description:
Share several ideas with another child about how to keep their block tower
from falling.

0678DEE3C8D542E4A2DE036BC2277666.description:
Stack blocks in several ways until they figure out how to make the tower stay
up.

AB583B10E50A42C696D026A823A6BB69.description:
Try to put a bead on a shoelace as a bracelet, and then look around for
other options to replace the shoelace when the bead doesn’t fit.

84F1B77C9B0D46748B7528D60EBDB510.description:
With support, explain how they decided that each child would get two
crackers from the snack tray. For example, by passing out one cracker to
each child, and then counting to make sure that there were enough left for
every child to have one more.

3C04BBEE09BD42F6B86C5BF6FFA0C35D.description:
Plan ways to solve problems based on their knowledge and experience,
such as getting a stool to reach a book that is on a shelf after trying to reach
it on tiptoes.

CF83BD3DECF349DC83A4F035744D013C.description:
With support and modeling, explain their thinking when trying to solve
problems, such as telling a familiar adult that they couldn’t put a toy back
together themselves, so now they are asking for help.

009DD9933A434F20A7C1D7DCB7D50F6A.description:
Try to fix things that are broken, such as putting a toy back together or using
tape to repair a torn paper.

D336B6205B864A9D9998E4E82DECBB1D.description:
Use a variety of strategies to solve problems, such as trial and error, simple
tools, or asking someone to help.

CE85C78278B84EBDA97C0B6E96239C16.description:
Develop an increasing ability to recognize mathematical problems in everyday situations at home
and in the learning environment, and experiment to find possible solutions.

17E1C74F36EF429C90B8651CE700CB04.description:
Begin expressing simple mathematical problems identifying mathematical
symbols such as “+” or “=.”

A628E949CDFC4B788D78FA90EF5A4C22.description:
Recognize different ways to represent number such as tally marks, dice,
5/10 frames, and numerals.

869CB69707E8483080E64E3B69120FF3.description:
Use mathematical terms like bigger/smaller than, more/less than or the
same when referring to quantities or size of items.

2C812E23FFB64374A2B2B438499EC2C2.description: Estimate how many toy frogs they think are in a plastic pond.

8F07833D035E4BB3A7D0051E675823ED.description:
Participate in a group activity to predict what will happen to a toy car if the
ramp is taller or shorter.

8FE11AF1C44E487C9953D6D6C07EDC6F.description: Tell about how they put a puzzle together.

15531213311446CEBE5289D2401BFFE2.description:
Point out pictures in book that resemble familiar shapes (e.g., sun/circle;
roof/triangle; truck/rectangle).

339782BD173B454BA1D21AE72A1F3EFF.description: Match numeral shapes when completing a number puzzle.

47892B9AAB04491D8CE421C13DA65044.description: Point to a clock and ask if it is time for snack.

AA51E2E4E4B34F87B53339B5FE73C97D.description:
Explore and begin to understand mathematical symbols and language in communicating their
explorations and discoveries.

2365D9EA692D46ADB04C33190EF4B4FA.description:
Explain to a friend how they figured out how many musical instruments were needed
so that each child in the group could have two.

0FAD66CF1BEB4B778664EB821B7C605E.description:
Count the children sitting at the table to answer how many napkins are needed for
snack.

27133759A5004B0298F0E9160EDEF438.description:
Use different size blocks, different arrangements, and other strategies to build and
re-build a structure that falls, until achieving their goal.

8D536C93CECB46B98F48C7C7915B8A10.description:
Suggest an idea for sharing when there are a limited number of scoops in the sand
table.

AF2CF3FA3A8442218D5DD1685B28ABA5.description: Make an ‘AB’ pattern using colored manipulatives.

0FA548731D294B30B23B705DDCE65AD6.description: Tell a friend that their birthday is in five days.

FE9135BEFF684C2AA7BEAE61DACC2F1B.description: Sort colored goldfish crackers, then count how many are in each color group.

4C8D6D3BC0A34CAD8D301B8F8CDE62FB.description:
When building with Legos, search for another wheel, while saying “I only have three
wheels.”

0E9926573423447088DF4FB9B4400591.description:
Play with signs, words, and patterns, e.g., Five Little Monkeys or Brown Bear, Brown
Bear, What Do You Hear?

A8E3A0E18D814C0DB9A7406290D79BD6.description: Ask a familiar adult to pour more milk to fill their cup all the way (concept of “more”).

CE5CD94393B14D6394A99EF49BC768EA.description: Ask for “three candles” on their birthday cake.

6D70A55E52884313BF0980223A53E3BB.description: Explore and begin to make sense of their world through mathematical thinking and strategies.

2E95FEB0481C48BCA29E5D9936696CC5.description:
Children begin to develop processes and strategies for solving mathematical
problems.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

CD9A2AC0EDAA4B108D848B6109B5566C.description: With modeling and support, remember that they should not share any personal information (name, age, address, phone number) online.

A7EA655E3E9848B4819038FD0BE317DE.description:
With modeling and support, use the share feature of a photo app to upload a
photo of their block tower to an archive managed by a familiar adult.

9E58955614394F2BAAED549D8F3BCCDF.description:
With guidance, remember to only open a web browser or internet-connected
software when an adult is supervising.

9B52B3AA377F404A9F2D1293AD737BAB.description:
With guidance and supervision, use only those websites listed in a web
browser’s bookmarks.

8E20DFEA7CDA44CB927615084E1F1FCC.description: Use a tablet to take pictures of themselves making different faces.

2D9376454AF3458EBD8559AC8B75F2E1.description:
Make suggestions about how to use the internet safely when the group is
deciding on expectations for their use.

4776A51CE87849948E40513F4938B544.description: Share pictures by showing the device to other children.

17C7C704BC874BEBA3B72A4D931E141B.description: Use only provided apps and digital resources on their device.

0804A920D1594AB3A955CDE7EEB47897.description:
Ask questions and engage in a conversation about how to use the internet
safely when the group is making a list of expectations.

4C0E6C8FA04A4826B30A77CE4BB3ED10.description: With adult guidance and supervision, begins to demonstrate an understanding of internet safety

04EF821F850C49678F1F3012840B0434.description:
With guidance and support, explain that a photo on the internet belongs to
the person who took the picture.

263CF16F2B374C3CA691217CD54698D6.description:
With support, use different apps on a device to take a series of photos of a
plant, and then include those photos in a slideshow of the plant’s growth.

ACEC9D24A4614083875F3325156586EF.description: With modeling and guidance, use a mouse to navigate a computer screen.

9DB2D635D2964C4F82CD53474CFD0FA6.description:
Make suggestions about how to use digital tools responsibly when the group
is deciding on expectations for their use.

A07BDDA6C8574A27B62071FF8DF280A4.description:
When reminded, and with modeling and guidance, plug a tablet into its
charger when they see a low battery warning.

0D948E578B604F228741079B7F4BA568.description:
With modeling and guidance, carry a device carefully around the room to
take photos.

5BF74327E83F47658B759A47FFBB9C06.description:
Ask questions and engage in a conversation about how to use digital tools
responsibly when the group is making a list of expectations.

7726B4FCD500444BA08FC728CEBF0648.description:
With modeling and practice, return a device to an adult when they see a low
battery warning.

CFABA4F48A5F4F6189987B3936258040.description: When reminded, shut down a device when they are finished using it.

D06E1359B4114AD1BA057001004DCCCF.description:
With modeling and guidance, turn a device on and off, and navigate to
favorite apps.

AB710C80DB0647FFB2B55D2DF1C13BC7.description:
When reminded, leave their food or drink on a table away from the device
they’re using.

08E24D10EFDD4F6C9E8F6438F7412C42.description:
Engage in a large group activity to make a short list of what is expected
when they are using digital tools in the learning environment.

95DF334B4CEC4BBA976F3F1266FA86C0.description: With adult support and supervision, uses digital tools and resources responsibly.

CC30C68B7D4345488818EB16EE659337.description: Children begin to use digital tools and resources responsibly.

CBC6DA9B1BED450D9D5FEDAEC800DE5B.description:
Use an encyclopedia app to answer their questions about where
penguins live.

4C968EAFA95F4604AB150B21EC9EA0E6.description: Record their measurement of the rain in their science journal.

5AD6F327952D4CC090EDB83135BA19BE.description:
Follow along with a simple YouTube Kids video as it demonstrates
how to draw a cat.

454799362FA54DB39675874A87B105CB.description: Show others a video they made of themselves dancing.

2442D6161262477DA197EDB08AD9A58B.description: Draw pictures of their bicycle with more and more detail.

3E0C3A915668406D8A7BC80EA5FCCF7E.description: Tell about something they learned from a video clip about penguins.

41319A4B00E444A3842C36AEA6B2B284.description: Use a tablet to take pictures of themselves making different faces.

8D6E2277630E4C9ABDE1C7DD5F6DB66A.description: Use adaptive devices for support when telling peers about themselves.

C40E910195A54EF09A1782BE3752B976.description: Show a familiar adult how they used scoops and funnels in the sensory table.

73F2C3E59F3A4631A41D2B7F48463A7B.description: Draw a picture of one of the characters from a favorite game.

6DD591CB31354F1CB7F2CF05C982708D.description: Describe a game they play on a family member’s phone at home.

630BE8CF471041989C6BFE410E2D89BB.description: Communicates about their experiences with (digital or non-digital) tools and resources.

F87DE606FBD34F1ABA2CF0701037D495.description: Use a cup, compass, or stencil to draw a circle.

8B498235D17F4F95AA054AE4B1298B6F.description:
With adult supervision, look up dinosaurs in an encyclopedia app to find out
what color dinosaurs were.

26AB0141BBF7486DBAE6CF5E9989BD7E.description:
Look through a book about birds to find out how many different colors a
parakeet can be.

73123C7D237849B2A3F831DB3FB9BC72.description:
With adult support, use non-standard measuring tools, such as blocks or
carpet squares, to figure out how long something is.

1EAF349B55C3497C8B9223D54A876414.description:
With adult support and supervision, use a computer to look up instructions
for how to plant seeds.

6AA10F2ECF4C40D983E6AEE477E9DA65.description: Look at a picture of a block tower as an example of what they can build.

CC26369634E84004A8B22A6E7C737FD7.description:
With adult support and supervision, use a tablet to look for pictures of a
plant’s life cycle.

1E36E970A9234BF89E0F217D35BD7F47.description:
With adult support and supervision, explores (digital or non-digital) tools and resources to find
information.

101916A74ECC4A3A9A07D9AE4BB18FC4.description: Children explore and interact with (digital or non-digital) tools and resources.

79D0BBAD7EFE4AC6AB9EA5ED5D6E91C3.description: Plan and build a complex block construction with other children.

DB4896A069714A80BDB1142F8505609E.description: Work as a group to draw a map on a tablet or chart paper.

13A49B0D1A314251AEB219B2DDCF6FB9.description: Take turns using a tablet with another child.

AFFD5625FC5940E78548C53CB789CEC9.description:
Use glue sticks, scissors, and paintbrushes to create a mural with other
children.

C7945557A5E44C08BC9FA81CF2537DAE.description:
Work with other children to use a tablet to collect data on their peers’ favorite
fruit.

B16168446DB142C9B1B8C5A19F62B825.description: Use a computer next to another child.

8B988F64C6134712ADADFCDBC28D2C08.description: Work with other children to take pictures for a collage.

4B03900132F8459EBCA5CE5AF0E67649.description: Uses tools to work with others.

FD91000F33C04BF09E3FB07D2CB57924.description:
Use a translation or interpreter app to help them communicate with a friend
whose home language is not the same as their own.

AA518B42810345B1B9464870EFFD059F.description:
Play a “coding” game using arrow cards to “program” another child’s
movements.

EE2BBBB924F047E085F6C400BECDB7ED.description: Join in with others of differing abilities in solving a puzzle or maze.

80C8B5939F8E4C8881B3C8EC6EDC12B5.description: Use adaptive devices to operate software on the computer.

E5DFF330FED544E9B3CB9BB1B184C7BB.description: Use a tablet to take pictures of themselves making different faces.

3243741405354E079ED835431B39B20D.description: Use a mirror to watch themselves make happy and sad faces.

2470D3BF69294DF6BBDCB4E7B3CEAC86.description: Explores tools for the purpose of communication or self-expression.

C3C085CF3FC44BF6AF8462B4C1138B9D.description:
Children use tools (digital or non-digital) to communicate and
collaborate with others.

241360A8790343FCAD71EEE75A4F07CF.description:
Ask a familiar adult to look up the directions for a card game they want to
play.

7BB4E0C86013400AAFCCDEBFB494D076.description: Think of and test several ways to build a sturdy ramp for their toy cars.

6B680BC78DCA4D4ABB6030A7BDC91E91.description: Ask a familiar adult to plug in a tablet that won’t turn on.

8005D8B7A3984E2C9253C61DDD28BA2B.description:
Walk around the room touching a magnet to different things to find out what
will stick to it.

CECD15CE7F5845049A1D65317D75FF7B.description:
With adult support, look through the basket of playdough tools to find
something that will cut playdough.

256AA835FDEF47DEB7786B993E2D42F6.description:
Recognizes real-world problems in their environment and begins to experiment with tools and other
strategies to solve those problems.

B62D20006677485AB272BD5B74ED2760.description: Experiment to discover what a magnet will stick to.

96D371B88CE040889EB6E6466E61A7EB.description:
Learn how to play Red Light, Green Light and explain the rules to another
child.

284ECF5297484FB7AD111CA135E466B1.description: Stop pouring milk into their cup before it’s full or overflows.

C2D51DAA0F8A449CBFA5DDEEBD050B4B.description: Add water to sand to make it moldable without turning into mud.

FF0CEDB2F54843559A091911213A07A3.description:
