Bounce balls on the sidewalk with more and more force, to get them to
bounce higher.

755A3FF524FA40099393ADBECB91053F.description:
Carry their toy cars to the hard floor or table to play “because they go faster”
than when they’re on the carpet.

1090F2B1EADE4AC39EE14B977AB96DA9.description: Learns from their experiments and experiences.

C8E73CAA855A4E9DAA5E67E7583461B2.description: Use an eyedropper to move liquid from one container to another.

E3C3BC28CB954E8C8BC5984F630B43E0.description: Use a stencil, straight-edge ruler, and/or compass to draw shapes on paper.

7C53EE0C791E47B5852BC428655AC2E1.description:
Use scrap supplies and paper to engineer an imaginary city. With adult
supervision, identify a website of their choosing from the options bookmarked in
the web browser.

4BAA90A19A1A466F8FDE6174BE0D6C62.description: Use a tablet to watch a video of how crayons are made.

CE5D61A09AD840CDA8FDDA04DD195F70.description: Use a tablet and stylus to “sign in” when they enter the learning environment.

AFBA35D9F18F4F0798D565032B0683FF.description:
Use a tablet, or clipboard and paper, to record other children’s responses to a
survey of their favorite colors, then use blocks or paper and markers to create a
graph to show the most common favorites.

D098BE220025494694235FECAE111A4F.description: Use a small garden trowel to dig holes for planting seeds.

C4CEA4C5164F4E8593130882C8BF8636.description:
Use a screwdriver to drive large, flat-tipped machine screws in and out of a
block of wood, using their fingers to twist and untwist a bolt on the other side of
the screw.

97124AAF5D544271A21AD8C74298AC8C.description: With adult supervision, choose a game from the PBS Kids website using visual cues.

241530261F0B48DCA2D136FEBC44E452.description:
Use a stylus to navigate an interactive technology device and find out how tall a
T. Rex was.

0A4881B9D1534ABF9855F4D880ADD2B6.description:
Make walls, tunnels, and towers for their castle construction with paper towel
tubes and cardboard boxes.

DD5EA225E66A40EFBA9FD56ADF649B96.description:
Use an empty cereal box to support an unsteady “balcony” area of the castle
they are building.

AA2ED46FD4044A889A1263F1C16F1994.description:
Work with a group to build a tunnel out of shipping boxes that is large enough to
crawl through.

20DB1C32160B40EC8D5DA50F4E95081A.description:
Record the behaviors of a classroom pet on a tablet, on chart paper, or in a
science journal.

F06BE5AB14DD40C1BCF4AB008E3B5089.description: Use a scoop to move water or sand from the sensory table into a container.

79AC2E39E96442EABD85FBA622BC828E.description: Use a small mallet or hammer to pound golf tees into a Styrofoam block.

8B475DBCC2354DB487E2D26813AC5687.description:
With adult supervision, click on a specific, favorite game app on a tablet in the
learning environment.

40124ED2BDBC46CE94BC319D700E8BF8.description: Use wooden blocks to build a road for the animal toys to follow.

341D33F39FBD4E5DB1364FB765F12487.description: Use wood blocks to make a ramp for cars.

9D761DF1D65B4DAEB6172BD06A2503D2.description: Use a large appliance box as a space for dramatic play.

B191FC75740A4383BE568117AD9CEE49.description: Use a triangular block as a ramp for a small car.

5D366B360F444D5DBB786E6549991D37.description: Use a sand timer to know how long their turn is on a computer.

2EB5D6DA83F44A5784870161258BD018.description: Use a camera to take a picture of their block tower.

67555D06AE3645789E7098F52112239D.description: Explore and experiment with different uses for the tools, objects, and materials in their environment.

B57A244A57EB4AC1AC9D25D3F67E3BEA.description:
Children use tools (digital or non-digital) to learn, create,
accomplish tasks, and solve problems.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

2452D80829B642ACAD2183A0803217B1.description:
Explain that plants and animals need food and water, but non-living things
like rocks and toy cars do not.

8726E9E96B88447BAE6D11CFE407C9C7.description: Ask a familiar adult if a caterpillar’s chrysalis is a living or non-living thing.

62130C1D92A8478DB8F06397D1850716.description: Mis-identify seeds or coral as “non-living” things.

12E14E0F4FA248A0AA7D3505DFE9D915.description: Sort pictures of plants, animals, and other objects into “living” and “nonliving” categories.

E52FD5AAED424EFFB1163BB7233B92FF.description: Mis-identify a dead plant as a “non-living” thing.

F55D07196B0B437FB5723B55C27B0F9E.description:
Categorize things as “alive” and “not alive,” sometimes. For example,
recognizing that a dog is a living thing, and a toy car is not.

05AF91C7C39F4B46B3EC4BDC0A72D510.description: Sort rocks or leaves by size, color, shape, or texture.

27AA903577BD42549553BF877FEFAC40.description: Participate in a group activity to categorize things as “alive” and “not alive.”

685D83876AEC4414B41D00552FD3BD10.description: Observe, describe, and compare the differences between living and non-living things.

94D4B3BD5037461B8E3BDF330CEDFD3A.description: Watch for animal tracks during an outdoor walk.

616DB73CDFC84FAFAE04865978FAF952.description:
Participate in a group project to draw pictures of animals that live in
their community, to paste where they have been seen on a map of their
community.

FE1126E437C5414988B264241948CA35.description:
Point out a bush on the playground that is the same kind as one in their
aunt’s backyard.

56DBB97E6CFC41618268842779948FDF.description: Identify the basic needs of plants (water, air, sunlight, and nutrients).

61B969425D7F4238AEE5AFD1B3154DBA.description:
Participate in a group discussion about where they have seen deer in their
community.

832AD6E2FF434636BD879C7E180F2D49.description: Tell about the frogs they saw during their visit to the lake.

8DE85DAFF8034696BD9A109AAF42C20F.description: Identify the basic needs of animals (food, water, air, and shelter).

FBBF79527CC645ECA272D660DF9734D8.description:
Explain that the park they like best is the one where they go to watch the big
fish in the pond.

9FED6391240048F08B687044143CDB97.description:
Compare and describe features of the environment, such as identifying one
lake as bigger than another.

CD44D698806E47E7BBA528DADDE73A78.description:
Observe and explore the habitats of a variety of plants and animals in their community (such as
wooded areas, parks, lakes, and streams).

F19E19D01BFC499AB6EB8CBB812FE8A8.description: Watch a deer run through a field and notice that it gallops like a horse.

4ABA94EEB4734FE2B4223D1AA5825573.description:
Describe or identify more details around the characteristics of plants and
animals, such as the breed of a familiar type of dog, the shape of a flower
petal or leaf, more detail around the colors in a butterfly’s wings, etc.

DC5242309C3C4346927B1466B6D29553.description:
Describe a caterpillar they saw outside and ask what kind of butterfly it will
turn into.

A9CB881E0FE54A9981428CFFBBC51FEB.description:
Begin to recognize and discuss the life cycles of different kinds of animals,
such as recognizing that a bird hatches from an egg, but cats give birth to
kittens.

8B975867D41D4D10BB73FC0686D44FBA.description:
Ask about different kinds of flowers, and compare different characteristics of
their seeds (size, color, shape, etc.).

14EAB83CE14B445A824661EE1CFBA138.description:
When drawing a picture of themselves at Halloween, draw trees with orange
and brown leaves.

1F6DBC6304874B779AD2AE49D36BA532.description:
Tell a familiar adult, “The tree’s leaves are red, but they were green before,”
and ask why.

CA2EC87D60E340B1B004E230688456F9.description:
Show interest in caring for the environment, such as asking to care for plants
or animals in the learning environment.

92059EBE84A4419597BCE71783C69EBD.description:
Identify more characteristics of animals and plants, such as the color of the
leaves and flowers of a particular plant, a dog’s ear shape, etc.

843BCAF04F924CB48DA7B81964ACE0A7.description:
With guidance and support, use their fingers to poke holes in soil for planting
seeds.

246437B0C03B4AC28E2D01AD189A71D2.description:
After an adult explains that a tree’s roots help it drink water, pour a cup of
water at the bottom of a tree to “help it drink.”

AA0ED52F1F7C47FCB6464362AA2D6B1A.description: Point at a bird on the playground and announce, “Birds eat worms!”

D847E3C6514A4786A351DE15BB96FDA4.description:
Explore, observe, notice, and describe a variety of plants and animals in their community, and their
life cycles.

48B083F5E58941439CEA2088217F893E.description:
Children show a growing understanding of scientific knowledge related to living and
non-living things.

AC524FD429544C69B5EF645EE03C49BE.description: Categorize types of weather by the seasons they typically happen in.

112E661475E146AE82E72CA841AB7D52.description: Participate in a group routine to chart the changing temperatures.

4D922A3CD86B40E4AF903CF26344E189.description: Point out that the leaves change color before they fall off the tree.

64AF13EDF0BB4636BFBE7621682A0C59.description:
Notice leaves falling from the trees and say that soon it will be time to go to
the apple orchard or pumpkin patch.

210E16DF813045038808B91371762E05.description: Point out the leaves falling in autumn and new buds and sprouts in spring.

26DF1ADF38E543A691C352EC2C599CA2.description: Notice snow on the ground and say, “It’s cold!”

584E78A472D64457A4AA1FE2B1207F59.description: Recognize and make connections between the seasons and their observable characteristics.

F896811F985C4CE7AEB640DF372E27C4.description:
Participate in a group routine to chart how many days each type of weather
has happened.

20DF361A3B504E0AAB38AAB696863CE4.description: Use a weathervane or windsock to figure out which way the wind is blowing.

9CCA3EC730A3401B82FC5062D92FCA06.description:
Describe the weather using more detail, such as “It’s only raining a little bit,”
or “It’s sunny now, but my momma says it’s going to snow later.”

B877E8B350A94F25B1660CC1D8350535.description: Participate in a group routine to identify and record the daily weather.

B61EFB311A294D98A97E3BA78348669D.description:
Identify appropriate clothes for different kinds of weather (shorts for sunny
days, rain jacket for rainy days, heavy coat for cold winter days, etc.).

9763C7960D0E4ECB85897EC55BB31286.description: Participate in a group activity to make a snowman.

8DDC95602CCA42A6B66CBDCAE61B478F.description:
Express disappointment when rain means they won’t be able to play on the
playground.

8B6DFE15374A47689B3DE4B34B281D79.description: Laugh and dance in the rain.

A2A29D9B1A4644478700FD4626AE0F77.description: Ask for sunglasses when it is sunny out.

52B02ADE8B6F4E41A1BB509FFC579DEB.description: Recognize and identify different weather conditions and the ways weather can impact their lives.

9B70D0FFE3FB41FB8006A819F57D4938.description:
Experiment with using soil, water, and other natural materials such as straw
and broken leaves to create mud bricks in an ice cube tray, then build with
them once they dry.

3535C12D428F4FB2BA36BBB5DF2C4FEA.description:
Shake several different kinds of rock in a container until the rocks begin to
grind together and produce new sand and soil, then discuss what happened.

66FEB06EAF6C4AD2815F2B3C8BCF802C.description:
Match color swatches with the different colors of soil and rocks they find on
the playground.

8B763B63D5B646DCB737A931F31D550A.description:
Use a magnifying glass to look closely at the dirt to see and identify grains of
soil, as well as tiny twigs, rocks, and sometimes insects.

25F15EA6D357481582D51FB56F88F66F.description: Sort rocks by size, color, shape, or texture.

974CD03B958F40DB9D511C48338E7F99.description:
Participate in a group activity to identify differences between a collection of
rocks.

6B312FD352974D9B9B4B74EFE473724C.description:
Match color swatches with the different colors of soil and rocks they find on
the playground.

B89B5E5E895B4FF4BA280336F9FC78AC.description:
Explore and recognize a variety of earth materials in their community (soil, rocks, water, etc.) and
their observable properties.

8DD25CE13A4B47838BF6FEBDFF6AA120.description: Children show a growing understanding of the scientific principles related to the earth.

39A93B50C6D14A659F5EE0C5BDD1EF3F.description:
Play an electronic Simon Says game and match the light patterns,
sometimes.

1A207C630B5E462999D7D639D52A9F16.description: Use a desk lamp to make shadow puppets.

51CF4EB02A2C45ED951E49270836C101.description:
Tap different things around the room using rhythm sticks to see how the
sound varies.

9BAA74760B7E42FEBB7D0F872FFDCEFD.description:
Layer red and blue translucent panels over each other on the light table
to make purple.

6EE6CD32696746DD82E5B8231E448B45.description: Ask for sunglasses to shield their eyes from the sunlight.

6D80B5D31A34426DBE137C551FEB662B.description: Use a variety of objects as drums.

8DB333BB767646E790DB882F180AECB3.description: Play with a child-size piano or keyboard.

85BAFD87F8B346BB9CCB9CAFD0E7A7CB.description: Play with toy drums or egg shakers.

FC1D8744D75A43D9867DBE326E956E79.description: Build with translucent colored blocks on the light table.

7CA6E9CAA8BE46E1A67E147B8738C3BD.description: Use the light switch to turn lights on and off.

D71AFD9C4E774261A420912EDABEE74E.description: Observe and explore light and sound.

47FE289B5E724C7BAA2A896D98899731.description: Notice that when rain freezes in cold weather, it turns into ice.

4935BFCEBDC54C0C9EDB3304669FAE56.description:
With adult support, sort and classify items such as a block, a cup
of water, and the air as solids, liquids, or gasses.

93E7EE40107F4BE1AC8A09C355EE5EC4.description:
Work with a group to shake a jar of heavy cream until it turns to
butter.

D4D8C61017B84DEB97AFA083BB20AA01.description: Explain that when ice and snow melt, they both turn into water.

172AF8434C9A42F7934301FE68027C93.description:
Participate in group discussions to identify items that fit into the
categories of solids, liquids, and gasses.

CF28E134000343D084CCE9378DDF8126.description:
Breathe onto a cold window so they can write their name in the
condensation.

E3418E689CDF4D0092B3CCB3005C369E.description: Use their hands to melt ice cubes in the sensory table.

603E3C8536B54B5385848D46E51C36FB.description:
Paint with ice cubes that have been made with drops of food
coloring.

97CF6F74E37D4BA69CB2B670CC4AB4D1.description:
Notice that snow is melting into water, while playing with snow
outdoors or in the sensory table.

D0FC2151460E4A1FB909D18963C376E7.description: Explore and observe the states of matter (liquids, solids, gasses) in their environment.

4467B4EA652B4868A9583CC3B6D7F3F6.description: Explore using a small pulley system to raise and lower toy cars.

87F1BEA4BD6843769748111B430D9CAA.description:
Drop a feather and a baseball from the same height and notice that the
feather falls slower.

F89A34BA8115488D9C651D641F0DF364.description: Build a marble run and make predictions about what pieces they can add to make the marble move faster or slower.

F0EFF1391231471280F6155AD65A6857.description: Build ramps for toy cars and experiment to see which car goes faster down the ramp.

C2A19AD0CFF7496286C698FB88B40032.description:
Explore and compare the ways objects move, including their speed, direction, and duration of
movement.

4B8DA73EC08E447CB63D07EEFAD61CDD.description: Children show a growing understanding of the scientific principles of physical science.

30441B907CEC4A0CBE90E1AD57FD3411.description: Record the height of their seedling in their science journal each day.

E36525A197FB4AAA9DC69141A9A89F1E.description:
Use a bar graph to chart favorite colors in the group and discuss the results
using terms like more, less, and equal.

6C8F339AC6894ABD884BDF18B1F61E27.description: Notice that the clouds are getting darker and say, “I think it’s going to rain.”

C963AC52601040909996206EAEF63877.description:
After being taught that a plant needs moist soil, touch the soil in a potted
plant and ask to water it because it’s dry.

926E6CF1C0F54A969EFAD58994F01D0D.description:
Notice that the classroom fish comes to the surface of the water when
people stand near the tank, and ask, “Why is he doing that?”

B4E7A2946D144ACFBBF67C50DC1678DB.description: Point out the tiny buds beginning to form on trees and plants in the spring.

8DEE8547B0724CF7B37E62702CD6EAAE.description:
Chart different kinds of weather with their group over the course of a week or
a month.

9BCC4C4941EE4A858EB7DBA03CD296CC.description:
Tell stories about the squirrels in their neighborhood eating the jack-o’-
lanterns and playing with the decorations.

0D34149BC23540B3963F54C009714BAB.description: Point out the squirrels gathering nuts and ask why they need so many.

3B1EFF1E99234E8A8D7A3F1961CAEDD1.description:
Chart their predictions about what color flower will grow from the seeds they
planted.

1CE9411D2DBC49778F6E7254639AB149.description:
Say, “It’s sunny–we can go outside!” or look out the window at the rain and
grumble, “But I wanted to go outside.”

599D66F7DF574F67844E658E0AE032CB.description:
Ask to feed the classroom fish when they come to school in the morning
because “it’s breakfast time!” or the fish usually gets fed in the mornings.

8F1DCAFC8E654596B4606BD36239EB6E.description: Communicate and/or record observations, questions, and predictions about their environment.

7059BE1189904EA3821CF99A6EA3B4C2.description: Collect leaves and sort by type of tree and/or leaf shapes.

296A7784148042AC9A8540C4C034A35E.description:
Classify items by their similarities, such as “all of these animals have fur, and
these ones over here have scales!”

CFEE6D791E764CABB65D759D1E181A39.description: Measure the growth of their seedling every day.

1342CEE45D2C436D8DD9155725D88364.description: Sort manipulatives into separate containers during clean up time.

3F069C0BEB6A4041B8BE83792A02C24B.description:
Sort buttons by feel, into piles of fabric-covered buttons and buttons with
holes.

64A784DD639848D48BBEA438BC5BB0EC.description:
Chart different kinds of weather with their group over the course of a week or
a month.

F875E36B09A34B38B5D5453862AA337F.description:
Make marks in their journal as they count how many children have yellow
shirts and green shirts, then compare how many there are of each color.

C772A9E98A63483ABC49655139512CCA.description: Sort animals by habitat (farm or forest, for example).

D00134BB88E84A738AB2D0F8B30A3E08.description:
Talk about cats and dogs and demonstrate an understanding that they are
different.

9584CC85FFF745FDBD70E951931B2ED5.description: Sort blocks by material (plastic/wooden) during clean-up time.

1508238DC4504A93A36184C13D9CA40F.description: Observe, compare, and classify objects and information.

0891ABA601A146F6AA4A85D7BF5C26D8.description: With adult support, mix vinegar into baking soda to make it fizz over the edges of the container like a volcano erupting.

2BE14268DB7D4451834205E22DFA4E38.description:
On a light table, stack a blue translucent square on top of a red one to make
purple.

2FB633F4B9904A9DBB1BC34721D37480.description: Use a flashlight to make shadows with their hands.

D50C65FA3CE9409A81C4CE735061EBBA.description: Melt ice cubes in their hands.

13346E8F90FD47AEB7B263E3A39B5E61.description:
Label the parts of a flower in a drawing, such as stem, petal, roots, and
leaves.

181B4639AE11458AAE8B009DF2799ED9.description:
Use magnifying glasses to observe plants and insects on the playground
and record their observations in a science journal, such as drawing a picture
of a grasshopper and writing, “The grasshopper has long spikey legs.”

F687DEF46D21412B8B04B071264ED1E1.description: Notice the different colors of the birds on the playground.

A2912F4E1EA04F86A7DB70B522FC077F.description:
Draw their observations of a seedling’s growth over time in their science
journal.

9819E4C2A6C74177A7F6C313D4D44A08.description:
Taste several varieties of apples and describe the differences in flavor, color,
and texture.

A665E65322B743F3AF54964D286179D6.description:
Take a nature walk around the outside of the building with an adult and ask
them to identify things.

871AB73ADA374D858F8A9F12DA78200B.description: Notice which side is lower/heavier when weighing rocks on a balance scale.

20FE304228A848B2878E742A4DBB1268.description:
Mix paint colors and notice the new color they create, saying, “I put yellow in
my blue – now it’s green!”

6E0B17DC1C1F46BFA07C413E538C72FD.description:
Wheel around the room with a magnet wand, testing different objects to find
out if they stick (are magnetic), and announce, “The toy car sticks, but the
blocks don’t.”

206E022D8D8B447FB3408E5378DC1D71.description:
Observe and discuss the movement of worms in the sensory table. Say,
“That bug is going over the other one!”

D6E490603E864F92B95DEC00F2416514.description: Build a snowman by stacking lumps of snow.

76C6421116EB47B4B726C81BDFC53C3D.description: Notice snow on the ground and say, “It’s cold!”

8793B20FFCF344509788F63589F83C84.description:
Observe and investigate their environment using scientific thinking, scientific vocabulary, and the
scientific method.

A982C0B21E99446AB44CC6839986D0B9.description: Children explore and demonstrate curiosity about the world around them.

document.title: Early Childhood Standards of Quality for Birth to Kindergarten

284F137866AF4977A83C5ABE0076B89A.description:
Participate in a group activity to line up pictures of themselves at various
ages in the correct order.

1AC595412D134C618D8BFDF42E3B7B8B.description: Use vocabulary about time with some accuracy.

68F9B42E3CC94D9EBFA90105D6468C45.description:
Tell about their family histories with some accuracy. For example: “Mommy
lived in Japan before but now she lives here,” “My grampa’s mom used to be
like the people in the book, but then she was free and she had my grampa,”
and “My papa’s family has lived here since always. His gramma and grampa
lived in the house next door!”

DF7E66704AFA469F916A020A4F84D1A9.description:
Tell about things that happened in the past, are happening now in the
present, or will happen in the future with accuracy. For example, “Mommy
lived in Japan before, but now she lives here,” “I’m going to softball
tomorrow night,” and “I’m going to go to kindergarten soon!”

3D6A2BDDF94245E48972C4A7A3E4ABC5.description:
Tell about things that happened in the past. For example: “I used to like
purple, but now I like pink,” “Nana hurt her hip but now she’s all better,” or “I
went to Disney World before.”

C21424F1968C497C824D459B09E4FE48.description:
Tell a familiar adult that they are going on a trip to see their grandmother
because “it’s going to be her birthday” or that they can’t go to gymnastics
tonight because “my teacher called yesterday, and she doesn’t feel good.”

558209CF7E6D4919860605EE4EAFCFC9.description: Put pictures of a story in the order they happened.

03CD3376ECCC4DEA9C360696B4CA416D.description:
Use terms like morning, afternoon, day, and night to talk about times of the
day, with some accuracy.

82CC7A6A556D484AB7132B0D993EE07B.description:
Begin to use terms like yesterday and tomorrow with some accuracy. For
example, saying “Tomorrow I go to Sunday School” on a Friday.

38CF5E3FCC654A1DA130B10CFEEEF532.description:
Imitate familiar home routines during dramatic play, such as singing a lullaby
when putting a baby doll to bed or asking another child to pass out plates
and cups while they “make dinner.”

A2D5BDE5A16B4F65A2567CC464DF7FAE.description: Refer to a picture schedule to find out what will happen today.

D36B427439B345398BCFC909B1AB6E34.description:
Anticipate familiar routines, such as putting away their coat when they come
inside, coming to the snack table after afternoon group time, or brushing
teeth after a meal.

BBC6BED179074FC888BAD007D4FB0338.description: Demonstrate a growing understanding of the passage of time as it impacts their lives.

D4B0487C51FB497C89A4C51BA2ADFC01.description:
Use toys and other materials to make representations of mountains, forests,
streets, and other familiar landmarks during pretend play.

E46A3209A9314B608B74FC13BF9B28DE.description: Use a map to figure out if their home is closer to the park or the school.

C25C09B8BC3C4626AD573E369DDD0816.description: Recite the name of the street they live on and the town they live in.

F3B3EFFA9FDF4276A3379F0041831373.description:
Use terms like left and right when describing where something is,
sometimes.

5992A61221264738AA13797BCF8F0338.description:
Use green and brown tissue paper to represent trees or broken mosaic
pieces to represent a mountain in their artwork.

3EB0D91AFE1445A49913C335C1CDEA04.description:
Show interest in geographical tools, such as globes, maps, and GPS/map
apps on a tablet.

8B01CAC1ADAB449F91694D68AF53D2EC.description:
Recognize and draw pictures of familiar places, geographical features, and
landmarks in their community.

E3DDB76759704E3CB7BE106C5C61DCB2.description: Explain where something is, using terms like near and far away.

23D0A82FA166481B8571812E8C1EFFD3.description: Put a drawing into their own cubby space, most of the time.

81DBE6A2947B49A2BB11A40B22264D5A.description: Say, “The park by my house has swings.”

58A3DEF13D7842B0B267D25314274A01.description: Point out familiar places during a drive or walk around their community.

E41D2E2EC4C945178F8D0B1568BF0C98.description:
Begin to identify, and use location vocabulary to describe, places and physical features in their
environment.

B00C730A10BC41AE9F3D7B0CAEC1AEEE.description:
Ask detailed questions about an animal visiting their learning environment,
sometimes.

2C3C1DAB5DDF4230AA73E86F36FFEC73.description: Track the growth of a plant in their science journal.

451642915EE04837970D47E623036679.description:
Participate in a group activity to wear gloves while carefully collecting
garbage on the playground, sorting items into trash and recycling.

FE771B691DCD4B5385484FE4F1CE3D9D.description:
Participate in a group activity to carefully catch a grasshopper in an insect
habitat, observe the grasshopper, and then let it go again.

7ACBF314DB114AD69EE7155571113C33.description:
Participate in a group activity to track the weather, temperature, or plant
growth over time.

CBB427E340654AA697C2FC3BF7F770F7.description:
With modeling and reminders, put extra paper into a scrap box, and plastic
cups in the recycle bin.

04EC8400D41546999174DBF2F5E24547.description: With modeling and guidance, bring the packaging from their snack to a garbage bin rather than letting it fall on the ground outside.

703DE8DF6E3A484F868D1A86A4BD23E6.description: Explore and learn how to respectfully interact with nature.

513C182BAF034B36AD921EC67C9FA28A.description: Children begin to understand their place and time in the broader world.

3720CA682AFD4B81B382753D78B905CC.description: Explain that they are saving their “birthday money” for a later purchase.

8F75C571992743B48D55060635F15BC6.description: Set aside a project to work on the next day.

9D6F4E4F8B124E099DFE19DDD0CC1EF9.description:
Describe their family members’ jobs with more detail (a general idea of
what they do or where they work), with some prompting, sometimes.

1A9F6861315245DA931D02BC88EA1E72.description:
Share something about their family members’ jobs, with prompting and
support.

F7457BA5CDFA41DEB32D91171ADB7D59.description:
Exchange “goods and services” (food, veterinary care, etc.) for pretend
money during dramatic play.

B9E9BD7DE921473783BB1E68E0BCB8A6.description:
Use costumes and props to explore restaurant, veterinarian, grocery
store, and other jobs with dramatic play.

7173309A554C49E7BA0F4B65888C4624.description:
With guidance, trade a blue dinosaur to another child in exchange for
the red dinosaur they want to play with.

B5E4A550143C479182478725D2EC2690.description:
With guidance and support, agree to share a basket of dinosaur toys
with another child.

D6F20874BDBB4D7380675F63209EA8CA.description:
Develop a growing understanding of value, as well as supply and demand, as they relate to sharing
and trading.

F8030C5700264B59A72B7769FF9E4B4B.description:
Describe how they rely on their family to have their needs met.
For example: “Daddy went grocery shopping” and “Nana has to
work late tonight, but we get to go to the park tomorrow.”

3EEF9B5306BF4F2D80E90143EF7876A3.description:
Recognize the difference between needing something and
wanting it.

E5EC9F8815D0492086495BC5331DA16C.description:
Compare people’s clothing to a dog’s fur – how it keeps them
warm, protected from the sun, etc.

526EA2688D21483B950E483673577A0F.description: Point out that animals need food and water just like people.

5E8902C6C19B4208ABC4A7CB731365D5.description: Help give a pet food and water.

789CBD99F4CF436AB820F6819DB07A3E.description:
Develop a growing understanding of what people need to thrive and the ways people fill
those needs.

0EBAA0C4800C4E80894E60B850DED045.description:
Get their naptime blanket out after they finish lunch,
anticipating the next step in their daily routine.

8429A4B0669E4ED5AFD3EB3135F24CC8.description:
Say, “I can do it,” when a familiar adult is looking for
someone to help with a task.

ED06B459DA9840A1818C4149E7E86DE3.description:
Point out the differences between routines and schedules
at home and at school, or other groups they are part of.

7990EFE3307D4462A63F6735CBE1CD0B.description:
Participate in different routines in different situations, such
as washing hands when they come in from the playground
at school but pulling out a wet wipe to wash hands at the
park.

2B2983EAEEE141ACAD0006DB649E9348.description:
Offer their help to a family member setting the table for a
meal, or a classmate cleaning up.

492689E6B66C453A8CEE1E689B1A54B5.description:
Participate in simple routines such as gathering for group
time, washing hands, or checking on a pet’s food, with and
without reminders.

CB9803D3F9204966976C798BF683E497.description:
Show a growing understanding of and participation with the expectations, boundaries, and
responsibilities in their family, learning environment, and community.

2F7BF2F14FF94930924D3501ADF67D44.description:
Children recognize the value in the contributions they, their families, and
others make to the community.

D22C12DDD63449A781D8007206FD35F7.description:
Bring a Mosaico or other game from their home culture to show and
share with other children.

CF3DC418E3AA4C8CB4F79DABA0902723.description:
Tell an adult visiting for lunchtime that “Charlotte can’t have the
meatballs.”

C6803B8E7E9145B08ED34A9A4AF79A26.description:
Recognize and point out differences between traditions at home and in
other places. For example: “I use chopsticks at home,” or “At home, we
say a prayer before we eat.”

39D0ED5D716545BAA8EF0063F68A5614.description:
In a group discussion about what everyone did over the weekend, tell
about going to Aunt Hazel’s for a birthday.

1A224A620B2B4553A002C3EAEE76CC0E.description:
With support, tell about some of their own family traditions, such as “We
go to shul and say Shabbat shalom” or “Mommy wears a headscarf.”

EA7CF3FE8CBA493A880DDF01AB8115EA.description:
Participate in the routines, customs, and traditions of their family and community, and develops an
awareness of and respect for the ways these can differ across settings, families, and cultures.

250C167F75CE4574B7246248A8FBE9CB.description:
Share stories about what they do with their community group, or as part of a
cultural tradition.

8C683E4F8A6B44A7AA7117D1AC12D773.description:
Say, “I can do it,” when a familiar adult is looking for someone to help with a
task.

F663348EFF3B4A2B92DD936391C7BCC0.description: Tell about what they did at a family gathering.

15DAD2BBC5A94A188A0FB3BFA17B47A9.description:
Offer their help to a family member setting the table for a meal, or a
classmate cleaning up.

6D363E9D71F3485AA4448E437C14DEBC.description:
Mention different groups they belong to in conversation. For example, “I
build with blocks at my preschool,” “My family doesn’t eat that food,” “I like to
play with Sharine and Lucy. They live in my neighborhood.”

321C46B8041A4A12A7BE37CA53E671F7.description: Share a food their family eats on special occasions.

937C9D0C54344AD580713B89B217E01A.description: Tell a familiar adult about their dance teacher.

70B2FAC0C892441597CC89177E07ECA2.description:
Play with blocks while telling about a visit with cousins when they played
with blocks together.

C0DE1DE571794BD581089E0C58198FA4.description:
Demonstrate a growing sense of belonging across their home, their learning environment, and their
community.

56DD49CC1AB04678B1216AE2192611EB.description:
Tell about playing in the backyard with their cousins, or about other family
relationships.

F23D8BD37E92436E845C491EC1071340.description:
Look at a friend’s drawing of their family and have a conversation about the
ways their families are different and the same. “I don’t have a dog like you.
I have an iguana named Princess.” And “Your mama wears a headscarf like
my mama!”

D19192AA1A184346AE88BBB4E5622FE3.description:
Point to people in a photo from a large family gathering. “That’s my Aunt Lily
and Aunt Gigi. This is Grampa Ed and my cousin Maia.”

6B9B3602E70A42BC96158DDE4986B399.description:
When participating in a group discussion about things to do in Fall, describe
their family’s Día de los Muertos traditions.

7E77A8EB5D6248DE9F2F4445C1074471.description:
Draw a picture of their babysitter and say, “I like him. He plays trucks with
me!”

6F61057BA47E482FBFA07EF013BA652B.description:
Share about the work the adult members of their family do. “Daddy goes to
work at the fire station and Nana stays home with me and my sister.”

DA94EE82F52B4061B7D12BEC8A1AF693.description:
Draw a picture of their family and dictate the name of each person so a
familiar adult can label the drawing.

607C1AE34C084E738342ADB98B6FD84A.description: Tell about building a sandcastle with their family.

27733F726F3E469685B7227322A826E2.description: Draw a picture of their family, including themselves.

2A1DFD3511A84AF3A50505E2E0D65069.description:
Hold a family member’s hand and lead them to their learning environment or
group.

77F584874345486B8339BAD29E462F26.description:
Ask a friend, “Is that a picture of your family? This one is a picture of my
moms and my brother.”

E7EDBF53FCCF42D89A4817243B0FB6DF.description:
Recognize themselves as members of a family and become aware of how families are alike and
different.

907EF29ABE8D4E74A35FD791E3C53020.description:
Compare their own family and cultural traditions to others’. For example:
“My family lights candles for Channukah but Laurie’s family has a tree for
Christmas.” Or “I like bacon, but Nyla doesn’t eat pork.”

F3A36C493F8E4129A2A5CAC8DA0D0EDA.description: Tell about and discuss events involving their family members.

BB84EF918FF14BB0A4C545B691DFD3C2.description: Recite their home address and/or phone number.

E57DF4965C4C41E7B54DAF4C090DA94B.description:
With support, identify some of their own and others’ character traits. For
example, “Salim is a good friend. Jordan is nice, too. Kiki talks loud.”

0BCCCF51846D45D4A79528B52725EBC8.description:
Recognize and describe similarities and differences in some of their own and
others’ physical characteristics, such as hair color, age, and relative height.
For example: “I’m taller than Miguel.”

109BB4ECDDA4458694EE3FE4B7C0C7CE.description:
Join in group conversations about children’s preferences in concrete
categories such as food, colors, play areas, etc. “I like playing in the art area.
Sometimes Layla will paint with me, but her favorite is the blocks.”

DB84F7DDB42A410F8E40254659B165C0.description:
With support, recognize the similarities and differences between their own
characteristics and preferences and those of others.

5B8935A911B44A918FDE25936BBEB9FA.description:
Identify some of their own physical characteristics, such as hair color, eye
color, and hair texture or length.

883D3491BE7B43588877240B2C475696.description: Recognize and respond to their own first/given and last/family name.

83CB5B23979347C8B1386C4B20885A7C.description: Recognize themselves as unique individuals and become aware of the uniqueness of others.

20B6C9D502F74DD8A3B5CC816EF998A5.description:
Children understand and respect themselves and others as individuals and as
members of a family, learning environment, and community.

document.title: Michigan Integrated Technology Competencies for Students

3C34BE274C3C4E32A9EB8AE767B5CC29.description:
Explore local and global issues and use
collaborative technologies to work with others
to investigate solutions.

BD82896AB07946A48565358F519704FD.description:
Contribute constructively to project teams,
assuming various roles and responsibilities to
work effectively toward a common goal.

85743C43A0124F8BA19E27B7B0D3AED4.description:
Use collaborative technologies to work with
others, including peers, experts, or community
members, to examine issues and problems from
multiple viewpoints.

AB5B89163741476E9C213497B3F24CEF.description:
Use digital tools to connect with learners from a
variety of backgrounds and cultures, engaging
with them in ways that broaden mutual
understanding and learning.

A4BC58530CF244D390EF7AFB9B5CAE04.description:
Global Collaborator: Students use digital tools to broaden their
perspectives and enrich their learning by
collaborating with others and working effectively in
teams locally and globally.

AAE6D8640C214D5B911C00146078AD3D.description:
Publish or present content that customizes
the message and medium for their intended
audiences.

4C7797C1F161457DAE7BCE257D3454B4.description:
Communicate complex ideas clearly and
effectively by creating or using a variety of
digital objects such as visualizations, models or
simulations.

A7FD26E629A24A38B89290D17C95B71F.description:
Create original works or responsibly repurpose
or remix digital resources into new creations.

B68CFD53E26F4E75834F77A2AD30365E.description:
Choose the appropriate platforms and tools for
meeting the desired objectives of their creation
or communication.

F8E6EC19A6794ABC99F5C33D562F70F4.description:
Creative Communicator: Students communicate clearly and express
themselves creatively for a variety of purposes
using the platforms, tools, styles, formats and digital
media appropriate to their goals.

A791A9EC5E574E3481D09A7D4DD088AA.description:
Understand how automation works and use
algorithmic thinking to develop a sequence of
steps to create and test automated solutions.

0983C52DA6F44331A089AF35B26E9FB5.description:
Break problems into component parts, extract
key information, and develop descriptive
models to understand complex systems or
facilitate problem-solving.

D8061B75DED04A24A9AE846444C11BF6.description:
Collect data or identify relevant data sets, use digital tools to analyze them, and represent
